about: Recurring symbols (the owner's rule 5). Source of truth; tools/content/symbols.py audits it and writes content/symbols.md. Scores 0-2: link (sound-alike or literal tie to the term), concrete, unmistakable, drawable (an image generator gets it right), sticky (remembered at first sight). A symbol is approved when every score is at least 1, the total is at least 8, and its anchor words are its own. Terms starting with '=' match only a keyword term that is exactly that word.

symbols.symbol: the HART Hotel: a narrow old hotel seen cut open like a doll's house, a stag's head (a hart) over its door; blue wing on the viewer's left = right heart, red wing on the right = left heart; glass-roofed atrium lobbies upstairs, engine rooms with ventilation fans downstairs; the party wall = the septum
symbols.why: hart = heart; one fixed map for every intracardiac lesson
symbols.notes: The stag's head is small; the building carries the meaning. Keep the colours (blue = right, red = left) in every picture: generators get colours right more often than left and right.

symbols.symbol: a glass-roofed atrium lobby on the upper floor of the HART Hotel
a ground-floor engine room of the HART Hotel with a huge ventilation fan and thick brick walls

symbols.symbol: the orca balloon sitting astride the party wall, half over each engine room

symbols.concept: Pulmonary stenosis, right ventricular outflow obstruction

symbols.symbol: the blue engine room with its walls swollen into thick red muscle
a raised beer stein, "Prost!", propping the duct-tape tunnel open
a leather belt buckled tight around the pipe of dollar bills
symbols.why: a band around the pulmonary artery

symbols.symbol: a hose joining the orca's flipper to the pipe of dollar bills

symbols.concept: Atresia (a valve or vessel closed from birth)

a vendor tossing Bing cherries through the hole under the dollar pipe
the orca and the dollar pipe swapped: the orca leaving the blue engine room, the dollar pipe the red one

symbols.symbol: both the orca and the dollar pipe rising out of the blue engine room
symbols.why: two outlets from the right ventricle

symbols.symbol: an iceman pushing blue blocks of ice back through the hole, from the blue side to the red
symbols.why: EISEN-menger = ice-man; blue (venous) pushed into the red side

symbols.concept: Fontan operation (venous blood to the lungs with no pumping ventricle)
symbols.symbol: a stone fountain in the hotel courtyard, fed by the blue wing's chimney, its water running straight into the pipes of dollar bills by gravity, with no pump
symbols.why: FONTAN = fountain (Italian fontana); a fountain flows with no pump, as Fontan blood reaches the lungs with no ventricle

symbols.symbol: an astronaut in a white spacesuit (John Glenn) bending the blue wing's chimney down and plugging it straight into the pipe of dollar bills
symbols.why: GLENN = John Glenn, the astronaut New York welcomed with a ticker-tape parade; he joins the chimney (SVC) to the money pipe (pulmonary artery)

symbols.symbol: a little plastic toy hippo wedged into a red wing shrunk to doll size
symbols.why: HYPO-PLASTIC = hippo + plastic; the red (left) wing is shrunk to a toy

symbols.symbol: one thick tree trunk rising from both engine rooms, astride the hole in the party wall, with the orca and the pipes of dollar bills branching off it
symbols.why: TRUNCUS = trunk: one trunk, all branches off it

symbols.symbol: a subway switchman pulling a big railway switch lever that swings the orca and the pipe of dollar bills back to their own engine rooms, the Liberty crowns riding along with the orca
symbols.why: SWITCH: the great arteries are switched back; the coronaries go with the new aorta

symbols.symbol: a giant squeeze bottle of yellow mustard drawing a thick mustard wall across the upper lobbies that crosses the two streams over
symbols.why: MUSTARD (the surgeon's name) = mustard; the baffle in the atria redirects the streams. Senning is the same idea

symbols.symbol: a round red party balloon on a string, yanked through the upper party wall so that it tears the hole wider
symbols.why: the procedure is literally a balloon pulled through the atrial septum

symbols.symbol: a huge ox wearing a clear oxygen mask
a man breathing fast into a brown paper bag

symbols.symbol: wooden blocks stacked inside the pipe of dollar bills, one block for each Wood unit
symbols.why: WOOD units = wooden blocks that resist the flow of money

symbols.symbol: a pirate shouting ARRR and dancing a wild jig out of step with the music
symbols.why: ARRR-rhythm-ia = a pirate's ARRR + a broken rhythm

terms: right ventricle to pulmonary artery conduit
symbols.symbol: a clear twisting waterslide tube from the blue engine room to the pipe of dollar bills
symbols.why: a conduit is a tube built to carry flow; a waterslide tube is the one nobody forgets

symbols.symbol: a child with bright blue (cyan) lips and fingertips

symbols.symbol: a gardener moving a red rose from the mouth of the pipe of dollar bills to the orca balloon's mouth

symbols.symbol: a pink pig

symbols.symbol: a tailor's big scissors snipping apart lips that have been sewn together
symbols.why: the fused commissures are cut apart like a seam

symbols.concept: subaortic (subvalvular aortic) stenosis, the subaortic membrane

symbols.why: a membrane hung just below the aortic valve

symbols.symbol: a sculptor chiselling a block out of the bulging lower party wall

symbols.symbol: the lower party wall swollen into the huge bulging biceps of a bodybuilder, crowding the red room's doorway to the orca
symbols.why: a muscle-bound septum that blocks the outflow

symbols.symbol: an ice-hockey goalkeeper slamming his big blocker pad against the puck

symbols.symbol: a canal (a channel) dammed by a spilled can of white chalky glue

symbols.symbol: a tight pearl necklace choking the orca balloon just above its mouth

symbols.symbol: a young lad sliding down the front of the Statue of Liberty's green crown

symbols.symbol: big green cabbage leaves laid as bridges over the tar-clogged spikes of the Liberty crown
symbols.why: CABG is said 'cabbage'; the leaves bridge the blocked parts

symbols.symbol: a heavy stone angel sitting on a man's chest
symbols.why: ANGINA ~ angel; the weight on the chest

symbols.symbol: a nightclub bouncer ejecting guests out of the red engine room's door, a counter showing the share thrown out
symbols.why: EJECTION = thrown out; the FRACTION thrown out with each beat

symbols.symbol: a man sitting on a mountain of white sugar cubes
a coiled metal Slinky spring pushed on a long wire into a clogged pipe to hold it open

symbols.symbol: the opened stern of a ship rotting with green mould along its white centre line
symbols.why: the sternotomy (the ship's stern) gone rotten

symbols.symbol: a green lima bean vine growing down from the chest wall onto the front of the Liberty crown
symbols.why: LIMA = lima bean; a living vine, not a cut-off piece

symbols.symbol: a chain of blue sapphires laid as a bridge over a clogged spike of the Liberty crown
symbols.why: SAPHenous = sapphire, blue like a vein

symbols.concept: gated equilibrium radionuclide study (MUGA, gated blood pool)
symbols.symbol: a big glowing green coffee mug filled slowly, drip by drip, over many beats
symbols.why: MUGA = mug; it is built up over hundreds of beats

symbols.symbol: one glowing green shot glass downed in a single gulp
symbols.why: the bolus is seen on its first, single pass

symbols.symbol: a bucket of ice-cold water full of bananas poured over the hotel so that its fans stop dead
symbols.why: the solution is cold and rich in potassium (bananas); it stops the heart still

symbols.symbol: a big pink bubble-gum bubble bulging out of a wall
symbols.why: a thin-walled bulge that can burst

symbols.symbol: a street-corner elevator platform stuck in its raised position
symbols.why: ST = STreet, elevation = ELEVATOR stuck up

symbols.symbol: a bright green Kawasaki motorcycle ridden by a feverish child
a glass snow globe glowing with green gamma rays
symbols.why: GLOBulin = globe; gamma = the glowing rays

symbols.concept: Ebstein's anomaly (tricuspid valve displaced down into the right ventricle)
symbols.symbol: Einstein, wild white hair, pushing the trident down into the blue engine room
symbols.why: EBSTEIN ~ Einstein; the tricuspid valve is pushed down into the ventricle

symbols.symbol: a fist punching a hole straight through from one pipe into its neighbour
a cement mixer roaring nonstop
symbols.why: a machine that never stops, through systole and diastole

anomalous origin of the left coronary artery
anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
symbols.symbol: Al Capone in a pinstripe suit bolting the left spike of the Liberty crown onto the pipe of dollar bills
symbols.why: ALCAPA ~ Al Capone, who puts the crown on the money

symbols.symbol: a man fainting backwards onto a red velvet couch

terms: aortic valve replacement for aortic stenosis
symbols.symbol: a dentist fitting brand-new dentures into the orca balloon's mouth
a black bowling ball rolling out through the pipes and knocking things over
symbols.why: em-BOWL-us = a bowling ball that travels and blocks

symbols.symbol: Pinocchio, his long nose growing, trembling all over in the upper glass lobby
symbols.why: FIB-rillation = fibbing, Pinocchio; he quivers, he never beats

symbols.symbol: harp strings tying the bishop's mitre down to the floor of the red engine room
symbols.why: CHORDae = the chords (strings) of a harp

symbols.symbol: soggy dollar bills dripping with water, spilling from the money pipes
a soft paper tissue box set in as the valve
symbols.why: TISSUE valve = a box of tissues: soft, wears out, needs no rat poison

symbols.symbol: a clanking little steel robot set in as the valve
symbols.why: a machine: lasts for ever, needs warfarin for ever

symbols.symbol: a rat in a soldier's helmet
symbols.why: WAR-farin = war; it began as a rat poison

symbols.symbol: a black umbrella snapping open
symbols.why: the stiff valve snaps open just after the second sound

symbols.symbol: a grey wolf digging a shortcut tunnel straight from an upper lobby down to an engine room, past the sparking bundle of branches
symbols.why: WOLFF = a wolf; the accessory pathway is his shortcut

symbols.concept: re-entry circuit (AV node re-entry and other re-entrant tachycardias)
symbols.symbol: a toy train (a little subway train) circling forever round a loop of two tracks, express and local
symbols.why: the impulse goes round and round a loop of two pathways

symbols.symbol: a green hedge maze grown across both upper lobbies, leading the beat from the top to the knot
symbols.why: the operation is named after the maze it makes

symbols.symbol: a blowtorch burning a spot black
symbols.why: tissue is burnt to stop it conducting

symbols.symbol: a wobbling ball of green jelly on a stalk, hanging from the clock on the party wall into the lobby
symbols.why: MYXO = mucus, slime: a jelly on a stalk from the fossa ovalis (the clock)

symbols.symbol: a red crab
symbols.notes: Lung cancer = the crab clamping a sack of dollar bills (the lung). Metastases are its baby crabs (own symbol, same family).

symbols.symbol: a raised drawbridge between the upper lobby and the engine room, so no signal can cross
symbols.why: the signal cannot cross from atria to ventricles

symbols.symbol: an orchestra conductor at the top of the blue lobby beside the chimney, beating time with his baton
symbols.why: the sinus node sets the time for the whole heart

symbols.symbol: a tennis player serving an ace at the US Open in Queens
a coal miner with a lamp on his helmet, pushing hard
a tall windmill turning its sails
symbols.why: MIL-rinone = a mill; amrinone its older twin

symbols.symbol: a strong Doberman dog pulling on its leash
a tall purple foxglove flower
symbols.why: digitalis comes from the foxglove (Digitalis purpurea)

symbols.symbol: a Prussian soldier in a spiked helmet throwing the city's gates wide open
symbols.why: nitro-PRUSSIDE = a Prussian; it opens the arteries (afterload)

symbols.symbol: a cowboy's lasso pulling water out of a flooded room
symbols.why: LASIX = lasso; it pulls the water out

symbols.symbol: a fast brown hare
symbols.why: HEpARin ~ hare: quick on, quick off

symbols.symbol: a small asp snake coiled round a white tablet
a brass ear trumpet held up to listen
symbols.why: the pacemaker listens before it beats

symbols.symbol: a big roller-pump truck parked beside the hotel, its hoses plugged into the chimney and the orca
symbols.why: the roller pump of the heart-lung machine takes over the circulation

symbols.symbol: a long sausage-shaped balloon inside the orca's belly, swelling when the fans rest and shrinking just before they push
symbols.why: a long balloon in the aorta that inflates in diastole and deflates before systole

symbols.symbol: a tin man with a clockwork heart
symbols.why: the man of tin who was given a heart

symbols.symbol: one single big engine room with no party wall, both lobby doors opening into it
a bicycle wedged in the orca's mouth, its two wheels for the two lips
baby crabs that have scuttled away from the mother crab and settled somewhere else

layers.meaning: offspring of the cancer crab that left it and grew elsewhere, as metastases leave the primary
layers.place: they sit far from the mother crab (the primary), on another sack, island or organ

symbols.why: the cancer's children, travelled away from it
symbols.notes: Same family as lung cancer (the crab) on purpose.

symbols.symbol: a cat slicing a long loaf of bread into very thin slices with one sharp claw

layers.sound: a CAT scan, as everyone calls it
layers.meaning: the scanner cuts the body into thin cross-sections, as the cat slices the loaf

symbols.why: CAT scan = a cat; tomography = slices
symbols.notes: Say 'thin slices of a loaf' so the cat is not just a pet.

symbols.symbol: a glowing puppy (a pet) sniffing out the spots that eat sugar cubes and making them glow

layers.meaning: FDG is sugar: tissues that eat sugar fast (cancer, infection) light up where the puppy sniffs

symbols.why: PET = pet; it finds sugar-hungry tissue
symbols.notes: Combined PET-CT = the cat and the puppy together.

symbols.symbol: numbered railway stations along a sea-train line that runs down beside the ribbed hose (the trachea) and forks under it

layers.sound: a lymph node STATION is a railway station
layers.place: each numbered station stands where its nodes lie: high ones near the top of the hose, 7 under the fork (the carina), 10 at the branches

symbols.why: the nodes are literally called stations; a line of stations keeps their order
symbols.notes: Paint only the one or two station numbers the question needs (words:).

symbols.concept: trachea, windpipe (and the carina where it forks)
symbols.symbol: a big ribbed hose of stacked white C-shaped rings that forks into two hoses at its lower end

layers.meaning: the windpipe itself: a ringed tube that carries all the air
layers.place: it runs down from the neck and forks into two at the bottom (the carina and the main bronchi)

symbols.why: the trachea is a ringed hose; its fork is the carina

symbols.symbol: a brass tuba riddled with holes, soft white cheese oozing from them

layers.meaning: the holes are cavities, the cheese is caseating necrosis

symbols.why: tuba = TUBerculosis; holes and cheese = cavities and caseation
symbols.notes: Miliary TB = the tuba spraying a fine millet of tiny seeds everywhere.

symbols.symbol: a long pink sofa stretched into a slide, down which food slides from the mouth to a cooking pot

layers.meaning: food slides down it into the stomach
layers.place: it runs down behind the ribbed hose (the trachea), through the deck (the diaphragm), into the cooking pot (the stomach)

symbols.notes: Say 'a long pink sofa stretched into a slide' so it reads as a chute, not a seat.

symbols.symbol: a big copper cooking pot that receives the food at the bottom of the sofa slide

layers.meaning: the pot where the food is churned and cooked, as the stomach digests
layers.place: below the deck (the diaphragm), at the foot of the sofa slide; pulled up into the chest it is the gastric conduit

symbols.why: the stomach cooks the food; first used in lesson 10 (the pot through the torn deck)

symbols.symbol: a drawstring purse-neck tied round the bottom of the sofa slide where it enters the cooking pot

layers.meaning: a ring that squeezes shut and opens, as the sphincter does
layers.place: exactly where the sofa slide (oesophagus) enters the cooking pot (stomach)

symbols.why: a sphincter is a purse-string ring

symbols.symbol: bubbling green acid soup splashing back UP out of the cooking pot into the sofa slide, scorching it

layers.meaning: acid stomach contents flowing the wrong way and burning the lining
layers.place: from the pot (stomach) back up into the sofa slide (oesophagus)

symbols.why: reflux = flowing back; the burn of heartburn

symbols.symbol: the lowest stretch of the sofa slide relined with wooden barrel staves, like the inside of a barrel

layers.meaning: the lining changed into another kind (metaplasia), as cloth changed to staves
layers.place: at the bottom of the slide, just above the pot, where the acid soup splashes

symbols.why: Barrett = barrel; the lining replaced near the GE junction

symbols.symbol: a golden chalice jammed in the drawstring at the bottom of the sofa slide, food piling up above it and the slide bulging wide

layers.meaning: the outlet does not open, so food piles up and the oesophagus dilates
layers.place: stuck in the lower sphincter (the drawstring)

symbols.why: achalasia = a chalice stuck in the outlet

symbols.symbol: the rim of the cooking pot folded up and wrapped round the bottom of the sofa slide like a scarf

layers.meaning: the fundus of the stomach wrapped round the oesophagus to stop reflux
layers.place: the pot's own rim (the fundus) round the foot of the slide

symbols.why: a wrap of the stomach round the oesophagus
symbols.notes: A partial wrap = the scarf only half way round.

symbols.symbol: a bushy pot of thyme growing at the very front of the chest cabin

layers.place: the thymus lies in the anterior mediastinum: the front of the cabin

symbols.why: thymus = thyme, and it sits in front
symbols.notes: A thymoma = the thyme bush grown huge.

symbols.symbol: a yellow excavator digging a deep hollow in the front of a treasure chest

layers.meaning: the front of the chest is dug in, hollow

symbols.symbol: a giant orange carrot standing upright as the pipe from the orca's arch up to the head

layers.place: it rises from the orca's arch (the aorta) up the neck to the head

symbols.notes: Carotid endarterectomy = the carrot slit open and its tar scraped out; carotid stenting = a Slinky inside the carrot.

symbols.symbol: a bandolier of brass AMMO rounds fired at the dancing pirate (the arrhythmia) to stop him

layers.meaning: an antiarrhythmic: it stops the pirate's out-of-step dance; stray rounds that lodge in the lung sack set its threads red-hot (pneumonitis)

symbols.why: amio = ammo; first used in lesson 25

symbols.symbol: the deck floor between the chest cabin above and the belly hold below, taut and springy like a trampoline

layers.meaning: a stretched sheet that bounces down and up with each breath
layers.place: the floor between the chest (above) and the belly (below); the sofa slide passes through a hole in it

symbols.why: the diaphragm is a domed sheet that moves with breathing
symbols.notes: First drawn as the deck in lessons 10, 56 and 68. Paralysis = the deck gone slack on one side.

symbols.symbol: the copper cooking pot pushing up through a widened hole in the deck floor (the diaphragm)

layers.meaning: the stomach slips up into the chest
layers.place: through the hole in the trampoline where the sofa slide passes; sliding = the drawstring rides up with the pot, paraesophageal = the pot rolls up beside the slide while the drawstring stays below

symbols.why: the stomach through the widened hiatus

symbols.symbol: a brown bear asleep in the hotel's engine room, turning the fan slowly while little coal reaches it, waking when the coal returns

layers.meaning: living muscle that slows down to match a poor supply and recovers when the supply is restored
layers.place: in the engine room (the ventricle), below a clogged Liberty crown

symbols.why: a hibernating bear: alive, slowed down, wakes up

symbols.symbol: a red crab spinning a thick grey rind, like a melon rind, all round the sack of dollar bills and the lining of the chest

layers.meaning: a cancer of the pleura that encases the lung in a rind
layers.place: on the lining of the chest and around the lung sack

symbols.why: the pleural rind of mesothelioma, spun by the cancer crab
symbols.notes: Same family as the crab.

symbols.concept: stenosis of a heart valve (aortic, mitral, tricuspid)
symbols.symbol: the valve's own door (the orca's mouth, the bishop's mitre, the trident) turned to grey STONE and pinched to a narrow slit, water squirting through it in one thin fast jet

layers.meaning: a stiff, calcified valve that opens only a narrow slit, so the jet is fast and the room behind it strains
layers.place: always on the valve's own symbol, so the reader knows at once which valve is narrow

symbols.why: sten = stone; stone = calcified and rigid; the slit = the narrow opening
symbols.notes: Older pictures (MedCosmos 41, 70, 72, 79, 113, 124, 126, 127; Johns Hopkins 131) show the door only pinched narrow, sewn or fused nearly shut, without the stone; new pictures add the stone. Rheumatic stenosis: the same, with the scarlet beads.

symbols.concept: valve regurgitation (insufficiency, incompetence): blood leaking back through a valve that does not close
symbols.symbol: a valve door that cannot shut, water GURGLING and spraying back through the gap into the room it has just left

layers.meaning: flow going the wrong way through a door that should be closed
layers.place: on the valve's own symbol (mitre, trident); the aortic valve keeps its own sagging, dripping orca mouth

symbols.notes: Ring stretched wide (functional regurgitation): show the valve's collar (annulus) pulled wide so normal leaves no longer meet. Earlier pictures: MedCosmos 65, 73, 74 (water spraying back past the trident).

symbols.concept: valve prolapse (mitral valve prolapse, Barlow's disease) and flail leaflet
symbols.symbol: one leaf of the bishop's mitre billowing up into the lobby above like a ship's SAIL full of wind; when a harp string has snapped (flail leaflet) the sail tears loose and flaps wildly

layers.meaning: a floppy, redundant leaf that bulges backwards past the closing line and lets water leak
layers.place: the mitre in the floor of the red lobby, bulging up into the lobby

symbols.why: a billowing sail = a billowing leaflet; a torn sail = a flail leaflet
symbols.notes: Posterior leaflet prolapse (the commonest in repair questions): the back leaf is the sail. Combine with gurgling water when it leaks.

symbols.symbol: a thick red muscular PILLAR rising from the floor of the engine room, the golden harp strings tied to its top and running up to the mitre (or the trident)

layers.meaning: a muscle column that holds the valve leaves down through the chords
layers.place: on the floor of the engine room under the valve

symbols.notes: Rupture after a heart attack (usually the posteromedial one, with a single blood supply): the pillar snapped, the mitre flapping loose. MedCosmos 105 and 140 drew it as 'the post'.

symbols.symbol: a brass COLLAR ring round the doorway of the valve; stretched wide it pulls the leaves apart, and in an annuloplasty a tailor sews a smaller brass ring in to draw the doorway tight again

layers.meaning: annulus is Latin for a little ring: the ring-shaped frame the valve leaves hang from
layers.place: round the rim of the valve's own symbol

symbols.notes: MedCosmos 42 (enlarging the aortic annulus) drew it as the orca's tight collar sawn open with a patch stitched in.

symbols.symbol: a ragged hole knocked through the thick brick LOWER PARTY WALL between the two engine rooms, water rushing through it

layers.meaning: a defect = a hole in the wall that should divide the two pumping rooms
layers.place: the lower (ventricular) part of the party wall; its height and nearness to the doors tells the type

symbols.why: hole in the lower party wall = VSD
symbols.notes: Type by place: perimembranous = high, beside a thin drum skin near the trident and the orca's mouth; muscular = low in the brick; subarterial = right under the pipe of dollar bills. Left-to-right flow: red water pouring into the blue room. Reversed: Eisenmenger's iceman. After a heart attack (ventricular septal rupture): the same hole, torn through the thin dead wall.

symbols.symbol: a hole in the thin UPPER PARTY WALL between the two glass-roofed lobbies, red water spilling through it into the blue lobby

layers.meaning: a hole in the wall between the two collecting rooms
layers.place: the upper (atrial) part of the party wall

symbols.why: hole in the upper party wall = ASD
symbols.notes: Each type keeps its own symbol: secundum = the clock in the middle; primum = the prime rib at the bottom; sinus venosus = the Venus statue at the top under the chimney; coronary sinus = the sink.

symbols.concept: atrioventricular septal defect (AV canal, endocardial cushion defect)
symbols.symbol: a big CROSS-SHAPED HOLE where the upper and the lower party walls should meet, with ONE shared door across it instead of the mitre and the trident

layers.meaning: the cushions that build the centre of the heart never formed: one hole above, one below, and a single common valve
layers.place: the very centre of the HART Hotel, where both party walls and both valve doors meet

symbols.why: a cross-shaped hole at the crossroads of the heart
symbols.notes: Cleft in the left part of the shared door: the door split in two. Common in Down syndrome. Partial AVSD = the primum hole alone (the prime rib).

symbols.concept: rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease
symbols.symbol: a long chain of SCARLET BEADS winding through the valve doors of the hotel, scarring and fusing them as it passes, the mitre worst of all

layers.meaning: streptococci grow in chains of beads; scarlet fever is their rash; years later the valves scar and fuse
layers.place: threaded through the valve doors, mostly the mitre, then the orca's mouth

symbols.why: a chain of scarlet beads = the strep chain behind rheumatic fever
symbols.notes: Rheumatic mitral stenosis: the beads fused into the stone mitre.

symbols.symbol: a set of FOLDED DENTURES carried up a fishing line from the groin and sprung open inside the old stone mouth of the orca, with no cut in the chest

layers.meaning: a new valve (the dentures of the AVR) folded small and opened inside the old one, through a catheter (the fishing line)
layers.place: inside the orca's own stone mouth

symbols.notes: Paravalvular leak: water gurgling round the outside of the dentures. Pacemaker after TAVR: the dentures pressing on the knot below.

symbols.concept: aortic root and the sinuses of Valsalva
symbols.symbol: three round bowls of red SALSA set round the base of the orca balloon just above its mouth; the green crown spikes rise from two of them, the third (non-coronary) holds none

layers.meaning: three pouches behind the three cusps; the coronary arteries arise from two of them
layers.place: the first part of the orca, between its mouth and the narrow waist above (the sinotubular junction)

symbols.why: Valsalva = salsa; three sinuses = three bowls
symbols.notes: Root dilation (Marfan, annuloaortic ectasia): the bowls swelling and stretching the mouth. Sinus aneurysm: one bowl bulging like bubble gum; rupture spills into the blue rooms.

symbols.symbol: a long ZIPPER torn open lengthwise between the inner and the outer skin of the orca balloon, water racing into the new channel between the two skins

layers.meaning: a tear in the inner layer lets blood split the wall into a true and a false channel, running along the vessel
layers.place: type A: the zip opens on the orca's front climb (ascending aorta); type B: only beyond its left flipper

symbols.notes: Malperfusion: the zipper's flap closing a branch (carrot, kidney beans, spaghetti, legs). Rupture into the aquarium round the hotel = tamponade, the commonest cause of death in type A.

symbols.concept: Bentall procedure (composite valve-graft replacement of the aortic root)
symbols.symbol: a big BENDY STRAW of white fabric with a set of dentures built into its lower end, put in place of the orca's mouth and root; the two crown spikes are sewn back onto it as round buttons

layers.meaning: one tube carrying a new valve replaces valve and root together, and the coronary arteries are re-sewn as buttons
layers.place: the first part of the orca, where the salsa bowls were

symbols.notes: Modified (button) Bentall: the round buttons. Mechanical valve: the dentures replaced by the little robot; tissue valve: the tissue box.

symbols.concept: valve-sparing aortic root replacement (David reimplantation, Yacoub remodeling)
symbols.symbol: young DAVID with his sling over his shoulder gently keeping the orca's own mouth and slipping a white fabric sleeve round it, the swollen salsa bowls trimmed away

layers.meaning: the patient's own valve is spared and re-implanted inside a tube; the dilated root is removed
layers.place: the orca's root and mouth

symbols.notes: Best when the cusps are normal (Marfan with a dilated root). Compare Bentall (the bendy straw), where the valve is thrown away.

symbols.concept: Marfan syndrome and other heritable connective tissue disorders of the aorta
symbols.symbol: a very tall, lanky wooden MARIONETTE with spider-long fingers and loose floppy joints, fanning itself with a huge CRIMSON FAN, its strings sagging; it sits astride the orca's swollen salsa bowls

layers.meaning: tall, long limbs, long fingers, lax joints: the connective tissue (the strings) is weak, so the aortic root swells and splits
layers.place: on the swollen aortic root

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins 92 drew it as a tall long-fingered man with a crimson fan: the same idea. Lens dislocation: a monocle slipping. Loeys-Dietz: the same marionette with twisted strings (tortuous arteries).

symbols.symbol: the whole HART Hotel, the orca and the head lantern frozen inside one giant ICE CUBE, the roller-pump truck switched off and silent, an hourglass running beside it

layers.meaning: the body is cooled deep, then all circulation is stopped for a limited safe time so the arch can be opened
layers.place: everything, the brain (the head lantern) included, inside the cube

symbols.why: frozen and stopped = DHCA; the hourglass = the safe time
symbols.notes: Cerebral perfusion during arrest: a thin hose still carrying cold water to the head lantern (forward through the flipper or carrot, or backward through the chimney).

symbols.symbol: a FROSTED THERMOMETER furred with ice, its red column sunk to the bottom, snow falling round it

layers.meaning: the body cooled below normal temperature to lower its oxygen needs
layers.place: standing beside whatever is cooled (the hotel, the head lantern)

symbols.why: a thermometer at the bottom = hypothermia
symbols.notes: Rewarming: the red column climbing again. Johns Hopkins 120 showed cooling on bypass as snow falling on the hotel and the head lantern.

symbols.concept: endovascular stent graft (EVAR, TEVAR) and endoleak
symbols.symbol: a coiled metal Slinky wrapped in white fabric, a SLEEVE, slid up from the groin inside the orca so it lines it and shuts the bubble-gum bubble off from the flow

layers.meaning: a stent (the Slinky) covered with graft fabric, placed from inside the artery, excludes the aneurysm
layers.place: inside the orca (thoracic or abdominal part), its ends landing in healthy wall

symbols.notes: Endoleak: water seeping round or through the sleeve into the bubble, which keeps swelling. Landing zones: where the sleeve's ends grip; covering the left flipper or the carrot needs a bypass first.

symbols.concept: artery of Adamkiewicz (blood supply of the spinal cord), spinal cord ischaemia, paraplegia
symbols.symbol: a little brown KIWI bird perched on the back of the orca low in the chest, feeding the long cable of the spine through a thin straw; when the kiwi starves, the legs below go limp

layers.meaning: the main feeder of the front of the spinal cord; lose it and the legs are paralysed
layers.place: springs from the back of the descending aorta, usually on the left, at the level of the 9th to 12th ribs

symbols.notes: Protection: a tap draining clear spinal fluid at the lower back (CSF drainage), keeping the pressure up, reattaching the kiwi's branches. Also after coarctation repair with long clamping.

symbols.concept: pericardium (the sac round the heart), pericardial effusion
symbols.symbol: a clear glass AQUARIUM built tightly round the whole HART Hotel, a thin film of water between its glass and the hotel walls

layers.meaning: a fluid-filled sac that wraps the heart
layers.place: round the whole hotel

symbols.notes: Effusion: more water in the tank. Pericardiocentesis: a needle draining the tank from below the breastbone. Window: a hatch cut in the glass so the water drains into the chest.

symbols.symbol: the glass aquarium round the hotel filling fast with RED WATER until it squeezes the hotel, the thin-walled blue wing caving in first; the pressure gauge sinks, the chimney bulges, the drums sound muffled

layers.meaning: fluid in a tight sac stops the heart from filling: low blood pressure, distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds
layers.place: inside the aquarium round the hotel

symbols.why: a flooding tank crushing the hotel = tamponade
symbols.notes: After heart surgery a single clot can press on one chamber only. Beck's triad was drawn in MedCosmos as a jazz trio of three brothers.
symbols.firstUsed: MedCosmos (a glass tank filling with red water)

symbols.symbol: a huge grey BOA CONSTRICTOR coiled tightly round the hotel's aquarium, squeezing it so the rooms cannot fill

layers.meaning: a thick, scarred, sometimes calcified pericardium that stops the heart from filling
layers.place: coiled round the pericardium

symbols.notes: Pericardiectomy: the snake cut off and peeled away. Causes: old surgery, radiation (violet rays), tuberculosis (the holed tuba).

symbols.concept: ventricular assist device (LVAD, RVAD, BiVAD) and mechanical circulatory support
symbols.symbol: a black-helmeted dark space knight in a long cape (Darth VADER), a glowing control box on his chest; his little pump is bolted into the tip of the red engine room and pushes straight into the orca, a cable running out through his skin to batteries on his belt

layers.meaning: a machine that keeps a failing heart alive; the driveline through the skin, the batteries on the belt
layers.place: the pump at the apex of the left ventricle, its tube into the ascending aorta

symbols.why: LVAD = Vader, kept alive by machines
symbols.notes: RVAD: the same knight on the blue side. Driveline infection: broccoli (the endocarditis cards' moss) where the cable leaves the skin. Pump thrombosis: a beaver's dam inside the pump.

symbols.concept: ECMO (extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, VA and VV)
symbols.symbol: a pair of big red fish GILLS in a clear box on a bedside trolley, a pump spinning beneath it, two hoses running into the patient's groin

layers.meaning: an artificial membrane lung, like gills, takes up oxygen outside the body; VA also pumps for the heart
layers.place: beside the bed, hoses to the groin (or neck): vein to artery (VA) or vein to vein (VV)

symbols.notes: VV: both hoses into blue pipes (lungs only). VA: blue out, red in (heart and lungs). Differential cyanosis on femoral VA: the head lantern blue while the legs are pink.

symbols.symbol: a gardener lifting a new organ, root ball and all, out of one terracotta FLOWERPOT and setting it into the space of the old one (a new HART Hotel, or a new sack of dollar bills)

layers.meaning: an organ moved from a donor (one pot) into a recipient (another)
layers.place: the new organ set where the old one was

symbols.why: transplant = moving a plant to a new pot
symbols.notes: Donor organ on ice: the pot in a bucket of ice. Earlier one-offs: a crane lowering a new red wing (MedCosmos 123), a new sack handed over at the gangway (Johns Hopkins 51).

symbols.concept: rejection of a transplanted organ (acute, chronic, antibody-mediated), bronchiolitis obliterans, allograft vasculopathy
symbols.symbol: an army of tiny white SOLDIER ANTS (the body's guards) swarming over the newly potted organ and biting its leaves brown

layers.meaning: the recipient's immune cells attack the graft as foreign
layers.place: on the transplanted organ in its flowerpot

symbols.why: soldier ants attacking the new plant = rejection
symbols.notes: Chronic lung rejection (bronchiolitis obliterans): the ants clogging the small twigs of the ribbed hoses. Allograft vasculopathy: the crown's spikes narrowed evenly along their whole length.

symbols.concept: cardiogenic shock, low cardiac output syndrome
symbols.symbol: the HART Hotel's LIGHTS GOING OUT one by one, its fans barely turning, a guest slumped grey and cold in the lobby chair

layers.meaning: the pump fails, so the body gets too little blood: cold, grey, confused, little urine
layers.place: the hotel itself (its power) and its guests (the body)

symbols.notes: Earlier pictures: MedCosmos 'the hotel's lights going out' (several), and 55 'fans stopped dead, a guest slumped grey'.

symbols.concept: atrioventricular (AV) node and the triangle of Koch
symbols.symbol: a big tight KNOT tied at the top of the crackling bundle of branches, sitting in the floor of the blue lobby between the coronary sink and the base of the trident

layers.meaning: the beat is held up there for a moment before it runs down the bundle
layers.place: the triangle of Koch: coronary sinus, tricuspid annulus and the tendon of Todaro

symbols.notes: Stitches near the knot (AVSD, VSD, tricuspid or aortic surgery) cause heart block: the drawbridge raised. Blood supply: usually from the right spike of the crown. MedCosmos and Shahzad used the knot many times.

symbols.symbol: a string of triangular SAWTOOTH BUNTING flags fluttering round and round the blue lobby in a perfect circle above the trident

layers.meaning: one big regular circuit in the atrium; the ECG shows sawtooth waves
layers.place: circling the tricuspid ring in the right atrium; the narrow isthmus between the trident and the drainpipe is where it is cut

symbols.notes: Ablation: the blowtorch burning a line across the isthmus so the circuit breaks. Compare atrial fibrillation (Pinocchio trembling).

symbols.symbol: Pinocchio, his long nose growing, trembling wildly all over INSIDE THE ENGINE ROOM, its big fan only shivering and pushing no water at all

layers.meaning: chaotic quivering of the ventricles: no pumping, death in minutes without a shock
layers.place: the engine room (ventricle), not the glass lobby

symbols.why: the same trembling Pinocchio as atrial fibrillation, moved down into the engine room
symbols.notes: Treatment: the jump-starting car's cables (defibrillation) or the bodyguard (ICD). Atrial fibrillation keeps Pinocchio in the glass lobby.

symbols.symbol: a car's TACHOMETER bolted to the engine room, its needle slammed deep into the red, the fan spinning to a blur

layers.meaning: the heart beating too fast
layers.place: on the engine room (ventricular tachycardia) or on the glass lobby (supraventricular)

symbols.notes: A re-entry circuit keeps its toy train; WPW keeps its wolf. The tachometer shows only the speed.

symbols.symbol: the engine room fans turning very slowly, the TACHOMETER needle sunk almost to zero

layers.meaning: the heart beating too slowly
layers.place: the same tachometer on the engine room, needle at the bottom

symbols.why: the same dial as tachycardia, needle at the bottom
symbols.notes: Causes: the conductor asleep (sinus node), the drawbridge raised (heart block), beta-blockers (the goalkeeper). MedCosmos 137 drew it as the fans turning very slowly.

symbols.symbol: a tiny BODYGUARD in a black suit living inside the hotel under its left eaves, jumper cables in his hands, watching the engine room and shocking the instant Pinocchio starts to tremble or the tachometer redlines

layers.meaning: a device that watches the rhythm and shocks a dangerous one
layers.place: under the left collarbone, its wire down into the right ventricle

symbols.notes: With pacing as well: the bodyguard also holds the drummer's sticks. MedCosmos used the bodyguard three times.

symbols.symbol: the crown's RIGHT SPIKE bending into a long RAINBOW arc round the right side of the hotel and down its back wall

layers.meaning: runs in the right groove round to the back; feeds the right ventricle, the inferior wall and, in most people, the conductor and the knot
layers.place: right side, then the back (posterior descending branch in right-dominant hearts)

symbols.why: the rainbow arc on the right
symbols.notes: Inferior heart attack (RCA): slow beats or heart block because the conductor and the knot lose their supply. Earlier pictures drew the crown's right spike (Johns Hopkins 129, 132; MedCosmos 69, 133).

symbols.concept: left circumflex coronary artery and its obtuse marginal branches
symbols.symbol: a CIRCUS ACROBAT FLEXing his body as he curls round the LEFT side of the Liberty crown to its back-left spike

layers.meaning: it bends round the left side of the heart in the groove to the lateral and back wall
layers.place: left side of the crown, back-left spike

symbols.notes: Its marginal branches: the acrobat's dangling legs. Easy to injure in mitral surgery (it runs next to the mitre's posterior ring).

symbols.concept: left main coronary artery and left main disease
symbols.symbol: a big cast-iron WATER MAIN with a red valve wheel, running from the orca's left salsa bowl to the crown and splitting there into the lad's slide and the acrobat; tar in the water main darkens both

layers.meaning: the single short trunk that feeds the whole left side; a block here starves a huge territory
layers.place: from the left coronary sinus to where the LAD and circumflex divide

symbols.why: a water main feeding the whole district
symbols.notes: Significant left main disease is a classic indication for bypass (the cabbage leaves).

symbols.symbol: a fizzing stick of NITRO DYNAMITE gently blasting a clogged or clenched pipe wide open, a soft pink headache cloud above

layers.sound: NITRO-glycerin = NITRO, the stuff of dynamite
layers.meaning: relaxes and opens veins most (less filling, less work), relieves spasm; headache and low pressure as side effects
layers.place: on the pipe it opens (veins, crown spikes, a radial graft in spasm)

symbols.why: nitroglycerin is literally what dynamite is made of
symbols.notes: MedCosmos used the dynamite stick six times.

symbols.concept: stress testing of the heart (exercise test, nuclear perfusion scan)
symbols.symbol: a man running hard on a TREADMILL in front of the HART Hotel while the Liberty crown glows; a dark cold patch appears where tar blocks a spike

layers.meaning: the heart is made to work hard so that a blocked artery shows itself (pain, ECG change, a cold spot on the scan)
layers.place: beside the hotel, the crown lit up above it

symbols.why: running on a treadmill = a stress test
symbols.notes: Nuclear perfusion: the crown glowing green, a dark spot that stays dark (scar) or fills in later (ischaemia, the sleeping bear).

symbols.concept: cardiac catheterization (right and left heart), pulmonary artery catheter
symbols.symbol: a long thin FISHING LINE paid out from a reel and threaded up from the groin through the pipes into the hotel, a pressure dial at its tip

layers.meaning: a thin tube threaded through the vessels to measure pressures and oxygen, or to inject dye
layers.place: in through the groin (or wrist, or neck) and up to the heart

symbols.why: a fishing line threaded into the heart
symbols.notes: With dye and pictures it becomes angiography (the photographer). MedCosmos drew a long thin probe on a reel.

symbols.symbol: a PHOTOGRAPHER squirting glowing MAGENTA DYE into the pipes and flashing his camera, so that only the pipes and their narrowings shine

layers.meaning: dye injected into vessels and X-ray pictures taken: shows the lumen and its narrowings
layers.place: on the pipes being shown (the crown, the carrot, the legs)

symbols.notes: Contrast kidney injury: the kidney beans shrivelling under magenta dye. MedCosmos and Johns Hopkins used the photographer.

symbols.concept: anomalous pulmonary venous connection (total and partial: TAPVC, PAPVC)
symbols.symbol: the pipes of green dollar bills coming back from the lungs gathered into one collecting pipe that pours out of a brass WATER TAP into the BLUE wing instead of the red lobby

layers.meaning: the pulmonary veins drain to the right side of the heart, not the left atrium
layers.place: supracardiac: the tap on the chimney; cardiac: on the coronary sink; infracardiac: below the deck, squeezed (obstructed)

symbols.why: the money pipes running to the wrong tap
symbols.notes: Partial (PAPVC): only one or two money pipes reach the tap, often with the Venus-statue hole (sinus venosus ASD). Scimitar syndrome keeps its own one-off sword.

symbols.concept: Norwood procedure (stage 1 palliation of hypoplastic left heart), Sano shunt, Damus-Kaye-Stansel
symbols.symbol: a NORWEGIAN WOODCUTTER in red flannel joining the big pipe of dollar bills to the little orca to make one wide new arch, and fitting a small hose to carry water on to the lungs

layers.meaning: the right ventricle becomes the systemic pump through a rebuilt arch; lungs fed by a shunt (BT hose or Sano tube)
layers.place: the arch, in a hotel whose red wing is a toy hippo's size

symbols.notes: Then the astronaut (Glenn) and the fountain (Fontan). MedCosmos drew the woodcutter twice.

symbols.concept: magnetic resonance imaging (MRI, cardiac MRI, MR angiography)
symbols.symbol: a giant red HORSESHOE MAGNET humming like a tuning fork over the thing it looks at

layers.meaning: a magnet and radio waves (resonance) make detailed pictures without X-rays
layers.place: hung over the organ being imaged

symbols.notes: Delayed (late gadolinium) enhancement: scar lit bright white under the magnet, living muscle dark. Pacemakers and the magnet do not mix. Johns Hopkins drew the horseshoe magnet twice.

symbols.concept: thrombus and thrombosis (deep vein thrombosis, left atrial thrombus, valve and graft thrombosis)
symbols.symbol: a BEAVER building a dam across the inside of a pipe out of little white plates and sticky red threads, the water backing up behind it

layers.meaning: a clot built in place, from platelets and fibrin, where flow is slow, the wall is damaged or the blood too thick
layers.place: where it forms: a leg vein (DVT), the left atrial appendage in AF, on a valve, inside a graft

symbols.why: a beaver's dam built in the pipe = a thrombus formed in place
symbols.notes: When a piece breaks off and travels it becomes the black bowling ball (embolism). Heparin (the hare) and warfarin (the rat) stop the beaver.

symbols.symbol: little round WHITE PLATES flying to a hole in a pipe and stacking over it to plug it

layers.meaning: they stick together to plug holes, the first step of stopping bleeding
layers.place: in the river of blood, gathering where a pipe is torn

symbols.notes: Few plates = bleeding (thrombocytopenia). The bypass machine chips and uses them up. HIT: the hare scattering the plates while beavers build dams everywhere. Aspirin's asp coils round the plates. MedCosmos drew little white plates.

symbols.symbol: two big hands PRESSING a tall porcelain VASE narrow at its waist, so the water in it rises

layers.meaning: they squeeze the vessels narrower so blood pressure rises (fingers, gut and kidneys may get less flow)
layers.place: on the pipes of the body

symbols.notes: Vasoplegia after bypass: vases gone limp and wide, needing the pressing hands.

symbols.symbol: BANANAS: piled high inside the rooms, only a few lying in the street outside

layers.meaning: bananas are the famous potassium food
layers.place: most potassium sits inside the cells (rooms), little in the blood (street)

symbols.notes: High potassium stops the heart (cardioplegia's bucket of bananas, asystole's nun); low potassium makes it irritable (Pinocchio, the pirate). MedCosmos and Shahzad used bananas several times.

symbols.symbol: a big old STEREO boombox whose volume knob is turned DOWN, silencing the red, hot, swollen noise of inflammation

layers.meaning: they turn down inflammation and the immune guards (side effects: high sugar, thin bones, poor healing, infection)
layers.place: beside whatever is inflamed or rejected

symbols.why: steroid = stereo; turning the volume down = suppressing
symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew the stereo twice.

symbols.symbol: the big round pressure GAUGE with its needle sunk deep into the low BLUE zone

layers.meaning: blood pressure too low
layers.place: the same gauge as hypertension, needle at the other end

symbols.why: the hypertension gauge, needle at the bottom
symbols.notes: Pairs with hypertension (needle in the red). Older MedCosmos pictures showed a dial sinking low, and once a drooping tuba (before the tuba became tuberculosis).

symbols.symbol: a big cluster of shining GOLDEN GRAPES

layers.meaning: staphyle is Greek for a bunch of grapes: the cocci sit in grape-like clusters
layers.place: growing on whatever it infects (the cards of endocarditis, the ship's stern, a graft, the chest)

symbols.notes: MRSA: the grapes behind a steel shield. Coagulase-negative staph (on prosthetic material): pale white grapes. MedCosmos drew golden grapes.

symbols.symbol: a red crab covered in silvery fish SCALES, sitting in the middle of the chest at the fork of the ribbed hose, pearls spilling from its claws

layers.meaning: a cancer of scale-like cells that makes keratin pearls; central, linked to smoking, can hollow out; may raise calcium
layers.place: central airways (lung), or in the sofa slide (oesophagus: upper and middle thirds)

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins 76 drew a red crab covered in scales in the sofa slide.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins 76 (a crab covered in scales)

symbols.concept: small cell lung cancer (oat cell carcinoma)
symbols.symbol: a red crab made entirely of OAT grains, sitting in the middle of the chest, scattering oats far and wide in every direction

layers.meaning: tiny cells, fast growing, spread early; treated with chemotherapy and radiation, rarely surgery; hormone syndromes
layers.place: central, near the fork of the ribbed hose

symbols.why: oat-cell carcinoma = a crab of oats

symbols.concept: carcinoid tumour (bronchial carcinoid, typical and atypical), neuroendocrine tumours
symbols.symbol: a wind-up TOY CRAB, red and shiny, sitting like a cherry inside the ribbed hose, blushing red when it releases its hormone

layers.meaning: a cancer-like tumour, slow and low-grade, often in the airway, can cause flushing
layers.place: inside a large airway, like a polyp

symbols.why: -oid = like: a toy that looks like the crab
symbols.notes: Typical: the toy wound down, slow. Atypical: the toy wound up tight, faster, can reach the railway stations.

symbols.concept: TNM staging of cancer (stage I to IV)
symbols.symbol: a winners' PODIUM with four steps numbered I to IV; the red crab stands on the step it has reached

layers.meaning: the higher the step, the more advanced and the worse the outlook
layers.place: T: a tape measure round the crab's shell; N: the railway stations it has reached; M: baby crabs far away

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew the crab on a podium step.

symbols.symbol: a chemist's flask of bubbling poison-green POTION poured into the river of blood, so it reaches every crab, big and baby, and scorches some of the healthy plants on the banks too

layers.meaning: a drug carried everywhere by the blood: it kills fast-dividing cells wherever they are, with side effects
layers.place: in the river of blood, reaching every site

symbols.notes: With radiation (chemoradiation): the potion and the violet rays together. Johns Hopkins drew a green or teal potion.

symbols.concept: radiation therapy (external beam, stereotactic body radiotherapy, brachytherapy)
symbols.symbol: a lamp shooting thin VIOLET RAYS from several directions so they cross on the crab

layers.meaning: beams aimed from outside; where they cross the dose is highest
layers.place: crossing on the target (stereotactic: many pinpoint rays on one small spot)

symbols.notes: Late effects: violet scorch marks on the crown, the valves and the aquarium (radiation heart disease). Johns Hopkins used violet rays several times.

symbols.symbol: a white delivery VAN carrying the green potion and the violet ray lamp: arriving AFTER the operation to mop up hidden crabs (adjuvant), or lit with pink NEON and arriving BEFORE the knife to shrink the crab first (neoadjuvant)

layers.sound: adju-VANt = a VAN; NEO-adjuvant = a NEON van
layers.meaning: extra treatment given after surgery, or (neo) before it
layers.place: parked outside the operating room, before or after

symbols.why: the van brings the extra treatment; neon = before

symbols.symbol: a deep-sea DIVER in a brass helmet diving down from a small notch above the breastbone into the dark middle sea of the chest, BESIDE (outside) the ribbed hose, his lamp lighting the railway stations

layers.meaning: a scope passed from the neck along the front of the trachea to take lymph nodes
layers.place: in front of and beside the trachea: stations 2, 4 and 7; it cannot reach 5 and 6 (the Chamberlain window)

symbols.why: a diver into the middle sea of the chest
symbols.notes: Compare endoscopy (a periscope INSIDE the sofa slide) and EBUS (the electric bus INSIDE the hose). The Chamberlain procedure keeps its own one-off (a chamberlain unlocking a window at the front left). Johns Hopkins drew a diver with a periscope beside the hose.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (a diver beside the hose)

symbols.symbol: an ELECTRIC BUS with a bat on its roof driving down INSIDE the ribbed hose, the bat's sound rings showing the railway stations outside the wall

layers.meaning: a bronchoscope with ultrasound (the bat) that sees and needles the lymph nodes through the airway wall
layers.place: inside the trachea and bronchi, next to the stations

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew the electric bus with the bat.

symbols.symbol: a lantern-tipped TELESCOPE pushed down INSIDE the ribbed hose: a straight steel one (rigid) or a thin bendy one (flexible)

layers.meaning: a scope looking inside the airways
layers.place: inside the trachea and its branches

symbols.notes: Rigid: for big bleeding, foreign bodies, coring out a tumour. Flexible: for looking, washing, biopsy. Johns Hopkins drew a steel telescope.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (a steel telescope down the hose)

symbols.symbol: a lantern on a slim telescope peeking in through a small KEYHOLE in the side of the treasure chest, lighting up the money sack inside

layers.meaning: operating inside the chest through small holes with a camera instead of opening it
layers.place: the side of the chest

symbols.notes: Compare thoracotomy (the chest's side lid flung open). Johns Hopkins drew the keyhole.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (a keyhole in the chest)

symbols.concept: upper endoscopy (oesophagoscopy, gastroscopy) and endoscopic ultrasound
symbols.symbol: a lantern on a PERISCOPE lowered INSIDE the long pink sofa slide (with a bat at its tip for endoscopic ultrasound)

layers.meaning: a scope looking inside the oesophagus and stomach
layers.place: inside the sofa slide

symbols.notes: Endoscopic ultrasound: the bat's rings measuring how deep the crab's claws reach and which stations are swollen. Johns Hopkins drew it this way.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (a periscope down the slide)

symbols.symbol: a PICKPOCKET lifting just ONE LOBE, one money bag, off the bundle by its string (the right sack is a bundle of three bags, the left of two)

layers.meaning: removal of one lobe of the lung, the standard operation for early lung cancer
layers.place: the money sacks: three lobes on the right, two on the left

symbols.why: taking one bag of the money = one lobe
symbols.notes: Sleeve lobectomy: the pickpocket also cuts a ring out of the ribbed hose and sews the ends together. Johns Hopkins 17 lifted one lobe out by its string.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins 17 (one lobe lifted out by its string)

symbols.concept: pneumonectomy (removal of a whole lung) and the postpneumonectomy space
symbols.symbol: a masked BANK ROBBER running off with the WHOLE SACK of dollar bills, the empty space behind him slowly filling with water

layers.meaning: removal of the whole lung; the empty space fills with fluid; higher risk, especially on the right
layers.place: one whole side of the chest

symbols.why: pneu-money-ectomy = the whole money sack stolen
symbols.notes: Right side riskier (bronchial stump leak: the fist; pulmonary oedema: soggy bills in the other sack). Extrapleural pneumonectomy keeps its own one-off (Johns Hopkins 104, 105).

symbols.symbol: a neat triangular CHEESE WEDGE cut from the outer edge of a money bag, the bag stapled shut behind it

layers.meaning: a small non-anatomic cut of the lung edge with staplers, for small peripheral nodules or diagnosis
layers.place: the outer edge of the lung

symbols.symbol: one ORANGE SEGMENT pulled cleanly out of a peeled orange along its own skin, its little stalk (artery, vein and airway) tied off

layers.meaning: an anatomic sublobar resection along natural planes, with its own vessels and bronchus divided
layers.place: inside a lobe of the lung

symbols.notes: Compare the wedge (a cheese wedge, cut across the natural lines) and lobectomy (a whole bag).

symbols.symbol: a single round silver COIN lying among the green dollar bills in the money sack

layers.meaning: a single round spot in the lung, classically called a 'coin lesion'; is it a crab or a harmless pebble?
layers.place: inside the lung (the money sack)

symbols.why: coin lesion = a coin among the bills
symbols.notes: Ground-glass: a frosted, see-through coin. Calcified and benign: a chalk-white pebble (Johns Hopkins). Growth over time: a stack of coins.

symbols.symbol: a red crab sitting on a stack of PANCAKES at the very top corner of the chest, its claws gripping the nerve wires running to the arm and the eye's little lamp beside it dimmed

layers.meaning: a lung cancer at the apex that invades the brachial plexus (arm pain), the ribs and the sympathetic chain (Horner: drooping lid, small pupil)
layers.place: the apex of the chest

symbols.notes: Treated with chemoradiation first (the neon van), then resection.

symbols.concept: FEV1 and pulmonary function tests (predicted postoperative FEV1)
symbols.symbol: a BRASS HORN blown as hard as possible for one second, a dial on its bell showing how much air came out

layers.meaning: the volume forcefully blown out in the first second: the main measure of airflow before lung resection
layers.place: blown from the money sacks up through the ribbed hose

symbols.why: one hard blast of the horn = FEV1
symbols.notes: Predicted postoperative: the same horn with some of its bags taken away. Johns Hopkins drew the brass horn.

symbols.symbol: grey puffs of smoke (carbon monoxide) passing through a fine FISHNET into a red river below

layers.meaning: how easily gas crosses the thin membrane between the air sacs and the blood
layers.place: the wall between the lung's air spaces (the net) and the blood (the river)

symbols.notes: Low DLCO: the net thick and clogged (emphysema, fibrosis). Johns Hopkins drew the fishnet.

symbols.concept: VO2 max (maximal oxygen consumption) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing
symbols.symbol: the huge OX in its clear oxygen mask galloping flat out inside a giant wooden TREADMILL WHEEL, a speedometer on the wheel showing its top speed

layers.meaning: the most oxygen the body can use at peak exercise (ml/kg/min): the best predictor of risk before lung resection
layers.place: the oxygen ox at full effort

symbols.why: the oxygen ox at full speed
symbols.notes: Above 20 safe; below 10 prohibitive. Johns Hopkins drew the ox in a treadmill wheel.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (an ox in a treadmill wheel)

symbols.symbol: a fat CIGAR puffing grey smoke into the money sacks and black tar into the pipes; for pack-years, stacks of CIGARETTE packs

layers.meaning: tobacco smoke: the cause of lung cancer and emphysema, and a risk factor for artery disease and poor healing
layers.place: its smoke in the lungs, its tar in the arteries

symbols.notes: Stopping (cessation): the cigar stubbed out in an ashtray, the date circled. Johns Hopkins drew cigars and packs.

symbols.concept: emphysema, COPD, lung volume reduction surgery
symbols.symbol: a money sack puffed up huge and full of holes like SWISS CHEESE, its bills torn into big empty spaces

layers.meaning: the walls between the air sacs are destroyed: big floppy air spaces, trapped air, a big chest
layers.place: worst in the upper lobes in smokers (lower lobes in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency)

symbols.notes: Lung volume reduction: trimming off the worst, holed top of the sack (Johns Hopkins 33). Giant bulla: the bull balloon.

symbols.symbol: a giant red inflatable BULL BALLOON swelling inside a sack of dollar bills and squashing the bills round it (small blebs: little calf balloons on the very top of the sack)

layers.meaning: a big air-filled space in the lung that compresses the healthy lung; a bleb bursting causes a pneumothorax
layers.place: inside the lung (bulla), on its top surface (blebs)

symbols.notes: Bullectomy: the bull balloon cut out so the squashed bills spring back. Johns Hopkins 35 drew the bull balloon.

symbols.symbol: a PUDDLE of water pooling in the bottom of the treasure chest round the money sack, lifting it up

layers.meaning: fluid between the lung and the chest wall, collecting at the bottom
layers.place: the base of the pleural space

symbols.notes: Haemothorax: a red puddle. Malignant: baby crabs paddling in it. Thoracentesis: a needle draining it. Johns Hopkins drew puddles.

symbols.symbol: thick yellow CUSTARD (pus) filling the bottom of the treasure chest like a custard PIE, a hard crust forming over the money sack

layers.meaning: infected, thick pus in the pleural space; later a peel traps the lung
layers.place: the pleural space

symbols.notes: Stages: thin puddle, then sticky with strands, then a hard crust (peel). Decortication: peeling the crust off the sack. Johns Hopkins 99 drew one puddle turned to thick yellow pus.

symbols.symbol: a clear BEACH BALL of air swelling inside the treasure chest, squashing the money sack flat against the middle

layers.meaning: air between the lung and the chest wall collapses the lung; under tension it pushes the heart aside
layers.place: the pleural space, usually from blebs at the top

symbols.why: a ball of air in the chest
symbols.notes: Tension: the beach ball pumped so hard it shoves the hotel to the other side and kinks the chimney. Johns Hopkins 97 drew an air balloon.

symbols.concept: chest tube (tube thoracostomy) and its underwater seal
symbols.symbol: a GARDEN HOSE coming out of the side of the chest into a glass WATER-SEAL bottle, bubbling when air escapes

layers.meaning: a tube draining air or fluid from the pleural space through a one-way underwater seal
layers.place: through the side of the chest wall (about the 5th space, mid-axillary)

symbols.why: a hose into a water bottle
symbols.notes: Air leak: steady bubbles in the bottle. Johns Hopkins drew a garden hose from a sailor's side.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (a garden hose from the side)

symbols.concept: chylothorax, chyle leak, the thoracic duct
symbols.symbol: a thin MILK pipe climbing up the back of the chest beside the spine; when it is cut, white MILK pours out and pools in the chest

layers.meaning: chyle is milky lymph full of fat; it leaks after injury to the thoracic duct
layers.place: the duct runs up on the right of the spine, crosses to the left about the 5th vertebra, and drains into the neck veins on the left

symbols.notes: Right-sided leak from low injury, left-sided from high. Ligation: tying the milk pipe low, just above the deck. Johns Hopkins drew the milk pipe.

symbols.symbol: a man coughing red into a brass SPITTOON that is filling fast

layers.meaning: blood coughed up from the airways; massive bleeding drowns the patient before he bleeds out
layers.place: from the ribbed hose and the money sacks

symbols.notes: Massive: lie the bleeding side DOWN, protect the good lung (a plug down the hose), then embolise the bronchial arteries.

symbols.concept: aspergilloma, Aspergillus and fungal lung infection
symbols.symbol: a tangled ball of green ASPARAGUS spears curled inside an old hollow cave in the money sack

layers.meaning: a fungus ball growing in an old cavity (after tuberculosis); can bleed heavily
layers.place: in an old cavity, usually in an upper lobe

symbols.notes: Often in the cave left by the holed tuba (tuberculosis). Bleeding: the spittoon.

symbols.symbol: a small walled CESSPOOL of thick festering yellow pus, bubbling, with a flat level line across it

layers.meaning: a walled-off collection of pus; on X-ray a cavity with an air-fluid level
layers.place: wherever it forms: in the lung, round a valve ring, in the head lantern

symbols.notes: Perivalvular abscess in endocarditis: a cesspool in the valve's collar, beside the cards. Brain abscess in cyanotic children. Johns Hopkins 26 drew a festering hollow cave.

symbols.symbol: a piece of a money sack locked in an iron JAIL CELL, fed by its own little pipe straight from the orca below

layers.meaning: lung tissue cut off from the airways, fed by a systemic artery from the aorta
layers.place: usually the left lower lobe; its artery from the descending or abdominal aorta (must be tied at surgery)

symbols.notes: Intralobar: the cell inside the sack, draining to the money pipes. Extralobar: a separate cell with its own wrapping, draining to blue systemic veins (azygos, the drainpipe).

symbols.concept: germ cell tumours of the mediastinum (teratoma, seminoma, nonseminomatous)
symbols.symbol: a big strange CRACKED EGG glowing at the very front of the chest cabin (a teratoma's egg has hair and teeth inside)

layers.meaning: tumours from germ cells (eggs and seeds of life), mostly in young men
layers.place: the anterior mediastinum

symbols.notes: Seminoma: a smooth white egg that melts under the violet rays and the potion. Nonseminomatous: a rough multicoloured egg; its markers (AFP, beta-hCG) are flags flying from the shell. Johns Hopkins drew a cracked multicoloured egg.

symbols.symbol: a swarm of BEES building a big honeycomb nest at the front of the chest cabin

layers.meaning: a cancer of lymphocytes; treated with chemotherapy and radiation, not surgery (surgery only for tissue)
layers.place: the anterior mediastinum and the lymph nodes

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew the bees' nest.

symbols.concept: neurogenic tumours of the posterior mediastinum (schwannoma, neurofibroma, ganglioneuroma)
symbols.symbol: a white SWAN nesting on the nerve wires against the BACK wall of the chest cabin, beside the spine

layers.meaning: tumours of the nerve sheath or the sympathetic chain, mostly benign in adults
layers.place: the posterior mediastinum, in the groove beside the spine

symbols.notes: Dumbbell tumour: the swan's neck poking through a hole into the spinal canal (operate with a spine surgeon). Neuroblastoma in children keeps its own one-off (a blast of neon light, Johns Hopkins).

symbols.symbol: a man whose eyelids droop shut and whose arms sink under a ladle of heavy brown GRAVY poured over him, a pot of thyme beside him

layers.meaning: muscles that tire and droop with use (eyelids, swallowing, breathing); linked to the thymus
layers.place: the thyme pot (the thymus) at the front of the chest

symbols.notes: Thymectomy helps (taking the thyme pot away); myasthenic crisis = he cannot breathe under the gravy.

symbols.concept: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous rupture of the oesophagus after vomiting)
symbols.symbol: a wild BOAR charging out through a burst in the lower left side of the pink sofa slide just above the deck, after the man has vomited hard

layers.meaning: forceful vomiting against a closed throat bursts the oesophagus; chest pain, air in the neck, sepsis
layers.place: the lower left side of the oesophagus, just above the diaphragm

symbols.notes: Other perforations (instruments, foreign bodies) keep the plain torn sofa slide (Johns Hopkins 71, 73, 74).

symbols.symbol: a freshly sewn seam between two tubes, a LEAKING SEAM dripping dirty water between its stitches

layers.meaning: the join between two sewn ends fails and leaks (after oesophagectomy: neck or chest; after lung resection: the bronchial stump)
layers.place: on the join itself

symbols.notes: Neck leak: a little drip handled by opening the neck wound. Chest leak: dirty water flooding the chest (sepsis).

symbols.concept: flail chest (paradoxical movement of a broken segment of ribs)
symbols.symbol: a medieval FLAIL: a loose spiked segment of the chest wall swinging on its chain, sucking IN when he breathes in and OUT when he breathes out

layers.meaning: several ribs each broken in two places: a free segment moves the wrong way; the lung bruise beneath is what harms
layers.place: the side of the chest wall

symbols.notes: Treat the pain and the lung bruise; fix the ribs in selected cases. A plain rib fracture keeps the cracked barrel staves (Johns Hopkins 6).

symbols.concept: thoracic outlet syndrome (neurogenic, venous, arterial), first rib resection
symbols.symbol: a wall OUTLET SOCKET at the base of the neck into which the nerve wires, the blue vein and the orca's flipper pipe are all crammed, pinched between the first rib and the collarbone

layers.meaning: the nerves, vein or artery to the arm are squeezed at the exit from the chest
layers.place: between the first rib, the collarbone and the scalene muscles

symbols.notes: Venous (effort thrombosis, Paget-Schroetter): the beaver's dam in the vein at the socket. Treatment: taking out the first rib.

symbols.symbol: a TELEPHONE CABLE running from the neck down the side of the heart's aquarium to the deck floor, ringing to make the deck bounce

layers.meaning: the nerve (C3, C4, C5) that drives the diaphragm; cut it and the deck on that side goes slack and rises
layers.place: down each side of the pericardium, in front of the lung root, to the diaphragm

symbols.why: phrenic = phone line to the diaphragm
symbols.notes: Injury: cold slush on the heart, a stretch or a cut near the aquarium; in children it can be serious (the deck flops and they cannot breathe).

symbols.concept: recurrent laryngeal nerve and hoarseness (vocal cord paralysis)
symbols.symbol: a brown HORSE whose long rein loops down under the orca's arch (on the left) or under the flipper (on the right) and back up to its throat; when the rein is cut the horse goes hoarse

layers.meaning: the nerve to the vocal cords; injury makes the voice hoarse and swallowing unsafe
layers.place: the left loops under the aortic arch by the ductus ligament, the right under the subclavian

symbols.notes: At risk in PDA ligation, arch surgery, oesophagectomy in the neck, left upper mediastinal node dissection. MedCosmos drew a hoarse brown horse.

symbols.concept: claudication and peripheral arterial disease (ankle-brachial index)
symbols.symbol: the Roman Emperor CLAUDIUS in his toga limping after a short walk, stopping to rub his cramping calf, then walking on

layers.sound: CLAUDication = CLAUDIUS (the lame emperor; Latin claudicare = to limp)
layers.meaning: calf pain on walking that goes with rest: narrowed leg arteries
layers.place: the calf; the narrowing is higher up (thigh or pelvis)

symbols.notes: ABI below 0.9: Claudius's ankle bracelet lighter than his arm bracelet on a scale. Rest pain and gangrene (critical ischaemia): his toes black and frosted.

symbols.concept: femoral artery and vein (groin access, femoral cannulation, femoral bypass)
symbols.symbol: a red pipe running down beside the long white THIGH BONE from the groin to the knee

layers.meaning: the main artery of the thigh; the usual door for catheters, cannulas and leg bypasses
layers.place: from the groin crease down the front of the thigh

symbols.notes: Femoral cannulation for bypass or ECMO: the hose entering at the groin; the leg below can starve (a second small hose feeding down).

symbols.concept: iliac arteries (aortic bifurcation, common, external, internal iliac)
symbols.symbol: the orca's tail splitting into two sprays of LILAC flowers, one down to each leg

layers.meaning: the aorta divides into the two iliacs (about the 4th lumbar vertebra), each splitting into external (leg) and internal (pelvis)
layers.place: the pelvis, at the end of the aorta

symbols.notes: Covering both internal iliacs with a stent graft: buttock pain (claudication) and gut ischaemia.

symbols.concept: mesenteric ischaemia (superior mesenteric artery, coeliac trunk)
symbols.symbol: a big MESSY plate of SPAGHETTI (the bowel) fed by a pipe from the front of the orca's belly; when the pipe clogs the spaghetti turns grey-black

layers.meaning: the bowel starves when its arteries block: pain far worse than the findings, or pain after meals and fear of food
layers.place: below the deck, the pipes leaving the front of the abdominal aorta

symbols.why: a messy spaghetti plate = the bowel and its mesentery
symbols.notes: Embolus (the bowling ball, from AF) or thrombosis (the beaver). After aortic surgery or long bypass: the spaghetti greying.

symbols.concept: kidneys and renal failure (acute kidney injury, dialysis, renal artery)
symbols.symbol: a pair of big red KIDNEY BEANS; failing, they shrivel dry and grey, and a washing machine (dialysis) churns the blood clean beside them

layers.meaning: the filters of the blood; low flow, dye and drugs injure them
layers.place: below the deck at the back, fed by short pipes from the sides of the orca

symbols.notes: Renal artery stenosis: a pinch in the short pipe, the beans shrinking and the pressure gauge rising. Dialysis access keeps the fist (arteriovenous fistula).

symbols.symbol: a big blue DRAINPIPE coming up from below the deck into the floor of the hotel's blue wing, opposite the chimney

layers.meaning: the great vein bringing blood back from the lower body
layers.place: enters the right atrium from below; the chimney (SVC) enters from above

symbols.why: drainpipe from below, chimney from above
symbols.notes: IVC filter: a kitchen sieve in the drainpipe catching the bowling balls. Cannulation for bypass: hoses into both chimney and drainpipe.

symbols.symbol: a chimney sweep's SCRAPER scraping the black tar (or old clot) out of a pipe that has been slit open lengthwise, then the slit sewn shut

layers.meaning: opening an artery and peeling out the plaque (or, in the lungs, the old organised clot) with its inner lining
layers.place: the carrot (carotid), the money pipes (CTEPH), the groin (femoral), the crown

symbols.notes: Carotid: the carrot slit open and scraped. Pulmonary: under the ice cube (circulatory arrest), the old bowling-ball clots scraped out of the money pipes. Johns Hopkins 147-150 drew the scraping.

symbols.symbol: a STARLING bird pulling a rubber band back: the further it stretches the band before letting go, the harder it snaps

layers.meaning: the more the muscle is stretched by filling (preload), the stronger the next beat, up to a limit
layers.place: inside the engine room, the band = the muscle fibres of its wall

symbols.why: the starling stretches the band = more filling, stronger beat
symbols.notes: Overstretched (a failing, dilated heart): the band frays and snaps weakly. Johns Hopkins showed resting length as a sailor pulling the fan's blades longer.

symbols.symbol: the heavy iron CITY GATES at the end of the orca that the red engine room must push its water through; half-shut gates = high afterload

layers.meaning: the resistance the ventricle pumps against after the valve opens
layers.place: the body's arteries beyond the aorta (the city)

symbols.why: the gates the water must push through
symbols.notes: Nitroprusside's Prussian soldier throws the gates open (afterload reduction). MedCosmos drew falling SVR as the city's gates swinging open.

symbols.concept: pulmonary vein isolation (and the box lesion)
symbols.symbol: the doorways of the money pipes in the red lobby each turned into an ISLAND by a moat of burnt black ground round it, so their wild sparks cannot reach the rest of the lobby

layers.meaning: a ring of scar round the pulmonary veins blocks the triggers of atrial fibrillation, which mostly start there
layers.place: round the four pulmonary vein openings in the left atrium (a box round all four together)

symbols.notes: Made with the blowtorch (heat) or the ice wand (cold); the core of every maze.

symbols.symbol: a balloon of thin white LACE blown up wider and wider, its skin thinning and straining at every hole of the lace

layers.meaning: wall tension rises with pressure and radius and falls with wall thickness: a wide, thin wall is under the most strain
layers.place: any round chamber or vessel: a dilated ventricle, an aneurysm

symbols.notes: Why big aneurysms burst and why a thick wall (hypertrophy) protects. MedCosmos drew a red balloon stretched wider, its skin thinning.

symbols.concept: cardiac output, cardiac index, stroke volume
symbols.symbol: a brass WATER METER on the orca where it leaves the hotel, its little wheel spinning to count the litres pumped each minute

layers.meaning: the volume pumped per minute (stroke volume times heart rate); cardiac index = per square metre of body
layers.place: where the orca leaves the red engine room

symbols.notes: Low output: the wheel barely turning. Shock keeps the hotel's lights going out.

symbols.concept: red blood cells, haematocrit, anaemia, haemodilution, transfusion, polycythaemia
symbols.symbol: little round RED DOUGHNUTS (red cells) floating in the river of blood; few of them, or the river thinned with water, and it turns pale pink

layers.meaning: the oxygen carriers; their share of the blood is the haematocrit; diluted by the bypass prime, crowded in cyanotic children
layers.place: in the river of blood

symbols.notes: Polycythaemia: the river thick and sludgy with doughnuts. Johns Hopkins showed haemodilution as plain water turning the river pale pink.

symbols.symbol: white SALT crystals: crowded in the street outside the rooms, rushing in through a fast revolving door when a beat begins

layers.meaning: the main salt outside the cells; its fast inward rush starts each heartbeat (phase 0)
layers.place: mostly outside the cells, in the blood (the street)

symbols.notes: Pairs with potassium (bananas inside the rooms). Lidocaine and class I drugs jam the salt's revolving door. MedCosmos drew salt crystals rushing in through a revolving door.

symbols.symbol: a cascading WATERFALL down which a waiter tumbles, throwing bouquets of COMPLIMENTS in every direction, each bouquet setting off red swelling where it lands
