layers.meaning: a cascade of blood proteins switched on when blood touches the bypass circuit: inflammation, leaky vessels
layers.place: in the blood flowing through the bypass circuit

symbols.notes: MedCosmos used this waiter four times.

symbols.symbol: a STUN GUN zapped at the engine room: its fan reels, dazed, cartoon stars circling it, though the coal is flowing again; it recovers by itself over hours to days

layers.meaning: after a short ischaemia with the blood flow restored, the muscle stays weak for a while and then recovers
layers.place: the engine room after the crown's flow has returned

symbols.notes: Compare the hibernating bear (asleep because the coal is still short; wakes when the flow is restored).

symbols.symbol: a small thin DRUM SKIN set into the party wall right under the orca's mouth, beside the trident's base and the knot

layers.meaning: the thin fibrous part of the septum; the commonest site of VSDs, close to the conduction tissue
layers.place: below the aortic valve, beside the tricuspid septal leaflet and the AV node

symbols.notes: Stitches here must avoid the knot (heart block). MedCosmos drew perimembranous VSD as a hole beside a thin drum skin.

symbols.symbol: small brass CANNONS pushed into the pipes and joined to the pump truck's hoses: one fires the pump's water into the orca, others draw the blue water out of the chimney and the drainpipe

layers.meaning: tubes that take blood out to the bypass machine and return it
layers.place: arterial: the orca (or the flipper root, or the groin); venous: the right atrium, chimney and drainpipe

symbols.notes: Femoral cannulation keeps the thigh-bone symbol for the place.

symbols.symbol: a giant pair of X-shaped iron TONGS clamped across the orca's front climb, cutting the hotel off from the flow, a stopwatch ticking beside them

layers.meaning: closing the aorta so the heart can be arrested and opened; the clamp time is the heart's ischaemic time
layers.place: the ascending aorta, between the crown's origin and the cannon

symbols.notes: Side-biting clamp: small tongs biting only an edge, for the vein grafts' top ends. Porcelain aorta: the tongs would shatter it.

symbols.symbol: a big ROLLING PIN rolling round and round over a clear tube, squeezing the water along it

layers.meaning: an occlusive pump: pushes a fixed volume whatever the resistance; it can pump air and burst a blocked line
layers.place: inside the bypass truck

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew the roller pump as a rolling pin squeezing a clear tube.

symbols.symbol: a fast-SPINNING CONE whirling the water outward into the tube, like a top

layers.meaning: a non-occlusive pump: flow falls when resistance rises; it de-primes with a big air bolus instead of pumping it; standard for ECMO and VADs
layers.place: inside the bypass truck or beside the ECMO gills

symbols.notes: Compare the roller pump (the rolling pin). Johns Hopkins drew a spinning cone flinging water outward.

symbols.symbol: a MAGICIAN's stage ACT: he pours blood into a glass while a huge stopwatch counts the seconds until it sets

layers.meaning: the seconds blood takes to clot: kept above about 400-480 on bypass, back near normal after protamine
layers.place: on the stage beside the bypass truck

symbols.symbol: a LION TAMER with a whip and a chair taming the fast brown hare (heparin) until it lies still

layers.meaning: a positively charged protein that binds and neutralises heparin after bypass
layers.place: given into the blood after the pump stops

symbols.notes: Reaction: low pressure, sudden pulmonary hypertension (the gauge on the money pipes jumping), allergy (fish allergy, NPH insulin, vasectomy).

symbols.symbol: a big red ANT in JOCKEY silks riding the brown hare; without its ant jockey the hare will not run

layers.meaning: heparin works only through antithrombin; low antithrombin = heparin resistance
layers.place: riding the heparin hare in the blood

symbols.why: the ant jockey rides the heparin hare
symbols.notes: Treatment of resistance: give the jockey back (antithrombin concentrate or fresh frozen plasma).

symbols.symbol: a SPOOL of sticky red thread unwinding to knit the white plates together into a firm plug

layers.meaning: fibrinogen is turned into fibrin threads that hold the platelet plug together
layers.place: in the blood, at the bleeding point

symbols.notes: Cryoprecipitate: a frozen spool. Low fibrinogen after bypass: the spool almost empty.

symbols.concept: fresh frozen plasma (FFP), prothrombin complex concentrate, clotting factors
symbols.symbol: a big yellow ICE LOLLY of frozen plasma, little red spools and tools frozen inside it, melting into the river

layers.meaning: the yellow part of the blood carrying all the clotting factors
layers.place: melting into the blood

symbols.notes: Prothrombin complex concentrate: the same factors squeezed into one small vial (fast warfarin reversal).

symbols.symbol: a big letter-K-shaped bunch of green KALE chasing away the rat in the soldier's helmet (warfarin)

layers.sound: vitamin K = KALE (green leaves are full of it)
layers.meaning: the liver needs it to make clotting factors II, VII, IX, X; warfarin blocks it, so vitamin K reverses warfarin slowly
layers.place: beside the warfarin rat

symbols.notes: Fast reversal before urgent surgery: the ice lolly or the vial (FFP, PCC); vitamin K takes hours.

symbols.concept: air embolism (massive air embolism on bypass, de-airing)
symbols.symbol: a big clear SOAP BUBBLE rolling through the pipes like a bowling ball and lodging in the head lantern or a crown spike

layers.meaning: air that enters the circulation and blocks small vessels (brain, coronaries)
layers.place: from the opened heart or the circuit into the orca, the head lantern, the crown

symbols.why: an air bubble travelling like the bowling ball
symbols.notes: Massive air on bypass: stop the pump, head down, clear the line, run the pump backwards up the chimney (retrograde cerebral perfusion), deep cooling. De-airing: shaking the bubbles out through a vent before the tongs come off.

symbols.concept: off-pump coronary artery bypass (OPCAB, beating-heart surgery)
symbols.symbol: an OCTOPUS gripping the beating hotel with its suckers to hold one spot still while cabbage leaves are laid, its fans still turning, the roller-pump truck parked with its engine off

layers.meaning: bypass grafting on the beating heart without the heart-lung machine; a suction stabiliser holds the target still
layers.place: on the surface of the beating heart

symbols.why: the octopus stabiliser is the real device's name
symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew off-pump as a small hotel with its fans turning and the pump truck idle.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (fans turning, the pump idle)

symbols.concept: clopidogrel and other P2Y12 antiplatelet drugs (ticagrelor, prasugrel), dual antiplatelet therapy
symbols.symbol: a pair of wooden CLOGS stamping CLOP-CLOP on the little white plates, cracking them so they cannot stick; before surgery the clogs are left at the door for five days

layers.meaning: blocks the platelets' P2Y12 receptor for their whole life; stop about 5 days before surgery (ticagrelor 3-5, prasugrel 7)
layers.place: on the white plates in the river

symbols.notes: With aspirin (the asp) = dual antiplatelet therapy.

symbols.concept: bivalirudin, argatroban and other direct thrombin inhibitors (heparin alternatives in HIT)
symbols.symbol: a big black LEECH clinging to the beaver's dam and dissolving its red threads

layers.meaning: blocks thrombin directly, without antithrombin; used for bypass in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia; no protamine reversal
layers.place: in the blood

symbols.symbol: an OVAL CAT FLAP in the upper party wall that swings open towards the red lobby whenever the blue side pushes harder

layers.meaning: a flap-valve opening left from fetal life; it opens when right pressure rises and lets a clot cross (paradoxical embolism)
layers.place: the middle of the upper party wall (fossa ovalis)

symbols.notes: A bowling ball slipping through the cat flap into the red side = paradoxical embolism. Compare the clock (secundum ASD: a real hole).

symbols.concept: left atrial appendage (LAA) and its closure
symbols.symbol: a floppy DOG'S EAR hanging off the red lobby, a dead-end pocket where clots settle; closed with a big clothes-peg clip at its base

layers.meaning: a blind pouch of the left atrium where most clots form in atrial fibrillation
layers.place: on the side of the left atrium, next to the crown's left spike

symbols.notes: In atrial fibrillation (Pinocchio) a beaver builds his dam inside the ear. Closure: clipped, stapled, sewn or plugged (Watchman).

symbols.symbol: a long-necked BRACHIOSAURUS rising from the first hump of the orca's arch, its neck splitting into the right flipper (arm) and the right carrot (head)

layers.meaning: brachio = arm, cephalic = head: it splits into the right subclavian and right common carotid
layers.place: the first branch of the aortic arch, on the right

symbols.notes: Cannulation for arch surgery is often here or under the armpit.

symbols.symbol: a blue pipe running ZIGZAG up beside the spine and arching over the right money pipe into the chimney

layers.meaning: drains the back of the chest into the SVC; with an interrupted IVC it carries the whole lower body
layers.place: right of the spine, arching over the right main bronchus into the SVC

symbols.notes: Tied in a Glenn if it would steal flow; divided in oesophagectomy.

symbols.symbol: a SECOND CHIMNEY on the left side of the hotel, its smoke running down into the sink in the blue lobby floor (coronary sinus)

layers.meaning: a left SVC kept from fetal life, usually draining into the coronary sinus (which is then wide)
layers.place: left side of the heart, into the coronary sinus

symbols.notes: It matters for retrograde cardioplegia (the sink leaks the banana juice up the chimney) and for Glenn operations (both chimneys need joining).

symbols.symbol: the SIDE LID of the treasure chest flung open on its hinges (a small hatch for a mini-thoracotomy)

layers.meaning: opening the chest between the ribs from the side
layers.place: the side of the chest, right or left

symbols.why: the chest opened from the side
symbols.notes: Compare the median sternotomy (the ship's stern opened down its centre line). Johns Hopkins and MedCosmos drew the side lid and the hatches.
symbols.firstUsed: Johns Hopkins (the side lid of the chest)

symbols.symbol: a small yellow SUBMARINE surfacing just below the tip of the breastbone, its periscope reaching up into the aquarium

layers.meaning: an approach just below the xiphoid to the pericardium (drainage, window) or the heart's underside
layers.place: below the tip of the sternum

symbols.notes: MedCosmos used the yellow submarine three times.

symbols.symbol: the bat (echo) sliding down INSIDE the pink sofa slide behind the hotel, its sound rings showing the hotel from behind

layers.meaning: an ultrasound probe in the oesophagus, right behind the left atrium: sharp pictures of valves, clots and the aorta during surgery
layers.place: inside the oesophagus, behind the heart

symbols.notes: Best for the left atrial ear (clots), the mitre, the aorta's dissection flap; blind to a small part of the upper ascending aorta.

symbols.concept: systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve, LVOT obstruction
symbols.symbol: UNCLE SAM in his star-spangled top hat grabbing the front leaf of the mitre and yanking it forward into the orca's doorway, blocking it and letting water gurgle back

layers.meaning: the anterior mitral leaflet is pulled into the outflow tract in systole: obstruction plus mitral regurgitation
layers.place: between the mitre's front leaf and the outflow to the aorta

symbols.notes: In HCM (the bodybuilder's wall) and after mitral repair with a long posterior leaflet or a small ring. Treatment: fill the room, slow the heart, stop inotropes; else revise.

symbols.symbol: a black BOW TIE stitched across the middle of the mitre so that it opens as two small holes instead of one

layers.meaning: the free edges of the two leaflets are stitched (or clipped) together in the middle, making a double-orifice valve
layers.place: the centre of the mitral valve

symbols.why: the repair's own nickname: the bow tie
symbols.notes: MitraClip: the same bow tie put in through the fishing line.

symbols.concept: Carpentier functional classification of mitral regurgitation (types I, II, IIIa, IIIb)
symbols.symbol: a CARPENTER at his bench sorting valve doors into three bins by how their leaves move: I normal (but a hole or a wide frame), II too much (prolapse), III too little (stuck: a in both phases, b only in systole)

layers.meaning: MR classified by leaflet motion: normal, excessive, restricted (IIIa rheumatic, IIIb ischaemic tethering)
layers.place: at the mitre

symbols.notes: Tethering (IIIb): harp strings pulled tight by a sagging engine room floor after a heart attack.

symbols.concept: mitral leaflet scallops and segments (P1, P2, P3; A1, A2, A3)
symbols.symbol: the back leaf of the mitre made of three SCALLOP shells side by side (P1, P2, P3), facing three matching segments of the front leaf

layers.meaning: the posterior leaflet has three scallops; P2, the middle one, prolapses most often
layers.place: the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve, P1 by the anterolateral commissure

symbols.notes: P2 prolapse: the middle shell billowing up like a sail; repair by cutting it out (resection) or new harp strings.

symbols.symbol: a DUKE in an ermine cloak reading a checklist: two big seals (positive blood cultures, a vegetation on echo) and a row of small ones (fever, risk, emboli, immune signs)

layers.meaning: major criteria: typical organism in blood cultures, echo evidence; minor: predisposition, fever, vascular and immunological signs
layers.place: beside the playing cards (endocarditis)

symbols.notes: Definite: 2 major, or 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor.

symbols.symbol: a chain of GREEN BEADS spilling out of a bad tooth into the river and coiling round a valve

layers.meaning: mouth streptococci, growing in chains; classic cause of subacute native-valve endocarditis after dental work
layers.place: from the mouth to the valves

symbols.notes: Same family as the scarlet beads of rheumatic fever (both streptococci in chains), told apart by colour.

symbols.symbol: a set of tiny CHILD-SIZE DENTURES fitted into the huge orca's mouth, the water squeezing through them

layers.meaning: a new valve whose opening is too small for the patient's body size: the gradient stays high
layers.place: the orca's mouth after valve replacement

symbols.why: dentures too small for the mouth
symbols.notes: Prevent it by enlarging the root (the orca's collar sawn open and patched) or choosing a bigger valve.

symbols.symbol: a human donor's own orca mouth and root taken out of a frosty tissue-bank FREEZER, ready to sew in

layers.meaning: a valve or root from a human donor, kept frozen; resists infection, needs no warfarin
layers.place: the aortic or pulmonary position

symbols.why: a valve from the human freezer
symbols.notes: Used for root abscess in endocarditis and to rebuild the right outflow (Ross, RV-PA conduits).

symbols.symbol: a bubble-gum bubble wearing a FAKE MOUSTACHE and glasses, bulging through a hole in the wall on a narrow neck, held only by the tissue round it

layers.meaning: a contained rupture: a hole through the whole wall, the blood held by surrounding tissue; tends to burst
layers.place: after a heart attack (LV), at an old suture line, at a groin puncture

symbols.notes: A true aneurysm (plain bubble gum) has all the layers of the wall and a wide neck.

symbols.symbol: a dark purple BLOOD BLISTER inside the orca's skin, with no zipper torn open

layers.meaning: bleeding into the aortic wall without an intimal tear; treated like a dissection of the same type
layers.place: in the wall of the aorta (type A if ascending)

symbols.why: a blood blister in the wall
symbols.notes: One of the three acute aortic syndromes, with the zipper (dissection) and the pothole (ulcer).

symbols.symbol: a deep POTHOLE eaten down through a patch of black tar on the inside of the orca's skin

layers.meaning: an atherosclerotic plaque that ulcerates through the inner layer into the wall; can bleed, dissect or rupture
layers.place: usually the descending thoracic aorta in elderly hypertensive patients

symbols.concept: elephant trunk and frozen elephant trunk
symbols.symbol: a grey ELEPHANT'S TRUNK of fabric hanging from the new arch down into the orca's tail (stiffened with a Slinky in the frozen version)

layers.meaning: a graft left dangling in the descending aorta at arch replacement, to make the later operation (or stent) easier
layers.place: from the replaced arch into the descending aorta

symbols.why: the operation is named after it
symbols.notes: Frozen elephant trunk: the end is a stent graft (the sleeve), done in one stage.

symbols.symbol: the orca balloon ripping open just past its left flipper, where its TETHER (the old duct tape) holds it down, as a car slams to a stop

layers.meaning: in sudden deceleration the mobile arch swings on the fixed descending aorta and tears at the isthmus
layers.place: the isthmus, just beyond the left subclavian at the ligamentum arteriosum

symbols.notes: Best seen on CT angiography; today mostly repaired with the sleeve (TEVAR).

symbols.concept: thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm and the Crawford extents (I to IV)
symbols.symbol: a CRAWLING baby inching down the back of the orca from the flipper towards the kidney beans, stopping at mile-posts I to IV

layers.meaning: an aneurysm spanning the chest and the abdomen; Crawford extents I-IV say where it starts and stops (II, the longest, carries the most paraplegia risk)
layers.place: the descending thoracic and abdominal aorta

symbols.notes: Spinal cord at risk: the kiwi.

symbols.symbol: the orca balloon turned to white PORCELAIN china, cracking if anyone clamps or cuts it

layers.meaning: a circumferentially calcified ascending aorta: clamping or cannulating it risks stroke and tearing
layers.place: the ascending aorta

symbols.notes: Options: no-touch (off-pump with no clamp), different cannulation, replacement under circulatory arrest, or TAVR (the folded dentures).

symbols.symbol: a long thin RADIO ANTENNA pulled out of the forearm and laid as a bridge over a crown spike, a nitro stick and a can of glue-blocker beside it to stop its spasm

layers.meaning: an arterial graft from the forearm, good long-term but prone to spasm (calcium blockers, nitrates); check the hand's other artery first (Allen test)
layers.place: from the forearm to a coronary artery

symbols.notes: Best on a tightly narrowed artery; competitive flow (a mild narrowing) closes it.

symbols.symbol: a smooth SATIN cloth wiping the yellow fat off the inside of the pipes and smoothing over the tar so it cannot crack

layers.meaning: lower LDL cholesterol and stabilise plaque; continued around CABG; side effect: aching muscles
layers.place: inside the arteries

symbols.symbol: a soft puff of NITRO SMOKE from the dynamite, breathed only into the money pipes, which relax wide open

layers.meaning: the very gas that nitroglycerin releases; inhaled, it opens only the lung vessels (pulmonary hypertension, RV failure)
layers.place: the pulmonary arteries, through the airways

symbols.notes: Stopping it suddenly: rebound (the gauge on the money pipes jumps); wean slowly.

symbols.symbol: a LION waking in its DEN beneath the crown: one roar stops the knot for a moment and every crown spike's tap swings wide open

layers.meaning: blocks the AV node for seconds (ends AV-node re-entry, unmasks flutter) and dilates the coronary arteries (stress tests)
layers.place: at the base of the crown, beside the knot

symbols.why: adenosine = a lion in its den
symbols.notes: MedCosmos drew the lion waking in its den.

symbols.symbol: a dentist's NUMBING NEEDLE jamming the fast revolving door so the salt crystals cannot rush in

layers.meaning: the dentist's local anaesthetic is also an antiarrhythmic: it blocks the fast sodium channel (ventricular arrhythmias)
layers.place: at the cell's sodium door

symbols.notes: MedCosmos and Shahzad drew class I drugs as the numbing needle.

symbols.symbol: a bright TROPICAL TOUCAN escaping through the broken window of a dying engine room, squawking the alarm

layers.meaning: released only when heart muscle cells die: the marker of myocardial injury and perioperative MI
layers.place: out of the damaged engine room into the blood

symbols.symbol: a BALLERINA spinning faster and faster on the POINTS of her toes in the engine room, her skirt twisting round and round

layers.sound: torsades de POINTES = twisting on the POINTS (pointe shoes)
layers.meaning: polymorphic VT twisting round the baseline, on a long QT; treated with magnesium, pacing faster, removing the cause
layers.place: the engine room

symbols.why: a ballerina twisting on her points
symbols.notes: Causes: low potassium (few bananas) and magnesium, drugs (amiodarone's ammo, sotalol), slow rates.

symbols.symbol: TWO DRUMMERS, one in each engine room, striking their drums at exactly the same moment so both fans push together

layers.meaning: pacing both ventricles together to correct the delay of left bundle branch block in heart failure
layers.place: a lead in the right ventricle and one on the left (through the coronary sinus or on its surface)

symbols.notes: With the bodyguard as well = CRT-D. A surgeon may place the left lead on the heart's surface through a small thoracotomy.

symbols.symbol: the glass aquarium round the hotel wearing a hot RED DRESS, steaming with fever and rubbing against the hotel like sandpaper

layers.meaning: inflammation of the pericardium (weeks after surgery or a heart attack): chest pain, fever, a rub, effusion; treated with NSAIDs and colchicine
layers.place: the pericardium

symbols.notes: It can fill the tank (tamponade) or, years later, harden into the boa constrictor.

symbols.symbol: a small pale SEA ANEMONE waving its fronds on a leaf of a valve door, bits breaking off and floating away

layers.meaning: a small benign frond-like tumour on a valve (most often aortic); its danger is embolism (stroke)
layers.place: on a valve leaflet

symbols.notes: The commonest valve tumour. Removed when it is mobile or has embolised, sparing the valve.

symbols.symbol: a soft white RABBIT nesting in the wall of a baby's engine room, slowly shrinking away by itself

layers.meaning: the commonest heart tumour of infants, linked to tuberous sclerosis; most shrink on their own
layers.place: in the walls of the ventricles

symbols.notes: Operate only if it blocks a valve or an outflow.

symbols.symbol: one big red crab made of tangled blood vessels, wearing a gold FIRST-PLACE MEDAL, clinging to the wall of the blue lobby

layers.meaning: the commonest primary malignant heart tumour; vascular, in the right atrium; poor prognosis
layers.place: the right atrium

symbols.why: the champion crab of the heart
symbols.notes: MedCosmos drew the crab with a gold first-place medal.
symbols.firstUsed: MedCosmos (a crab with a gold medal)

symbols.symbol: a CYCLONE wrapped in a crisp TACO shell, sweeping the white soldier ants off the transplanted plant while wringing the kidney beans dry

layers.meaning: the main anti-rejection drugs: they switch off T cells; they harm the kidneys, raise pressure and sugar
layers.place: over the flowerpot

symbols.symbol: the orca balloon CUT IN TWO at its arch, a clear gap between the halves, the tail half fed only through the duct-tape tunnel

layers.meaning: no continuity between the ascending and descending aorta; the lower body lives on the ductus (prostaglandin)
layers.place: type B (commonest, with DiGeorge) between the left carrot and the left flipper; A beyond the flipper; C between the two carrots

symbols.notes: Almost always with a VSD.

symbols.symbol: SAINT GEORGE on his horse riding past an EMPTY pot of thyme and a knocked-over can of glue

layers.meaning: no thymus (weak immunity: irradiated blood only), low calcium (the glue), conotruncal heart defects (truncus, interrupted arch type B, tetralogy)
layers.place: beside the arch or trunk defect

symbols.symbol: three identical FOOTBALL SHIRTS all numbered 21 hanging side by side on a washing line beside the cross-shaped hole

layers.meaning: an extra chromosome 21; about 40 percent have heart defects, most typically the AV septal defect; early pulmonary hypertension
layers.place: beside the AVSD (the cross-shaped hole)

symbols.symbol: a single TURNIP carved into the letter X, sitting beside the rope that pinches the orca's waist

layers.meaning: one X chromosome only: short girls; coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection
layers.place: beside the coarctation (the rope)

symbols.symbol: a cheerful ELF at a cocktail party, chatting to everyone, wearing the tight pearl necklace that chokes the orca above its mouth

layers.meaning: elfin face, very friendly, high calcium; supravalvular aortic stenosis and narrowed pulmonary branches (elastin gene)
layers.place: the necklace just above the aortic valve

symbols.why: the elf with the pearl necklace

symbols.symbol: a man HOLDing a RAM by its curly horns with an odd finger-like thumb, beside a hole in the upper party wall

layers.meaning: an inherited defect of the thumbs and forearms with an ASD (or VSD) and conduction problems
layers.place: beside the upper party wall

symbols.concept: vascular ring (double aortic arch, right arch with left ligamentum)
symbols.symbol: two orca arches (or an arch and its duct-tape tether) closing a RING round both the ribbed hose and the pink sofa slide, tight as an iron key ring, so the child wheezes and chokes on food

layers.meaning: arch vessels encircling the trachea and oesophagus: noisy breathing, difficulty swallowing
layers.place: round the trachea and oesophagus at the top of the chest

symbols.why: a ring round the hose and the slide
symbols.notes: Usually divided through a left thoracotomy (the side lid). MedCosmos drew a double arch as two orcas closing a ring.

symbols.concept: pulmonary artery sling (and complete tracheal rings)
symbols.symbol: the left pipe of dollar bills looping like a SLING round the back of the ribbed hose, between the hose and the sofa slide

layers.meaning: the left pulmonary artery arises from the right one and loops behind the trachea; often with complete tracheal rings
layers.place: between the trachea and the oesophagus

symbols.notes: Complete rings: the ribbed hose made of full O-rings (no soft back wall), narrow (slide tracheoplasty).

symbols.symbol: an old TREASURE MAP whose many winding dotted paths run from the orca's back to the sacks of dollar bills

layers.meaning: many collateral arteries from the descending aorta feed the lungs when the pulmonary artery is atretic (pulmonary atresia with VSD)
layers.place: from the descending aorta to the lungs

symbols.notes: Unifocalisation: gathering all the paths into one road (one pulmonary artery).

symbols.symbol: a round brass PORTHOLE window cut between the orca and the pipe of dollar bills, just above their mouths

layers.meaning: a hole between the ascending aorta and the main pulmonary artery: a big left-to-right shunt
layers.place: between the two great arteries, above both valves

symbols.notes: Closed early with a patch, before pulmonary vascular disease (the wooden blocks) sets in.

symbols.symbol: a THIRD ATRIUM LOBBY made by an extra glass partition across the red lobby, the money pipes pouring into the upper part and only a small hole letting the water through

layers.meaning: a membrane divides the left atrium; the pulmonary veins drain above a narrow opening (like mitral stenosis)
layers.place: inside the left atrium, above the mitre and the dog's ear

symbols.notes: MedCosmos drew the third lobby.

symbols.concept: congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (L-TGA)
terms: congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
symbols.symbol: the HART Hotel standing before a big MIRROR: in it the engine rooms AND the outflow pipes are both swapped, so the water still ends up in the right place (two wrongs make a right)

layers.meaning: both the atrioventricular and the ventriculoarterial connections are discordant: physiology is corrected, but the right ventricle pumps to the body
layers.place: the whole heart

symbols.notes: Problems: the systemic right ventricle fails, the trident leaks, heart block (the drawbridge). Double switch = sending both back.

symbols.symbol: the right pipe of dollar bills curving down like a giant Turkish SCIMITAR sword through the deck into the drainpipe (IVC)

layers.sound: SCIMITAR = the sword's shape on X-ray
layers.meaning: partial anomalous drainage of the right lung into the IVC, with a small right lung and often a systemic feeding artery
layers.place: right side, down through the diaphragm into the IVC

symbols.notes: MedCosmos drew the scimitar sword.

symbols.concept: aberrant right subclavian artery (arteria lusoria), dysphagia lusoria
symbols.symbol: a JESTER in a belled cap playing a trick: the right flipper pipe sneaking out last from the orca's arch and crossing BEHIND the pink sofa slide, pinching it as food goes down

layers.sound: LUSORIA = a jest, a trick (Latin lusus)
layers.meaning: the right subclavian arises last from the arch and runs behind the oesophagus; it may cause difficulty swallowing
layers.place: behind the oesophagus

symbols.notes: Kommerell's diverticulum: a bulge (bubble gum) at its origin.

symbols.symbol: a frosted ICE WAND pressed against the wall, freezing a white line of frost through it

layers.meaning: freezing the tissue to make a scar line that blocks electrical conduction (maze lines, round valve rings)
layers.place: on the atrial walls, the mitral and tricuspid rings

symbols.notes: Compare the blowtorch (radiofrequency heat ablation).

symbols.concept: parachute mitral valve and Shone complex
symbols.symbol: the bishop's mitre hanging from a single PARACHUTE: all its harp strings gathered to ONE pillar

layers.meaning: all the chords insert into a single papillary muscle: mitral stenosis; with supravalvar ring, subaortic stenosis and coarctation = Shone complex
layers.place: the mitral valve and its pillar

symbols.notes: Shone: the parachute, a ring above the mitre, the shower curtain below the orca's mouth and the rope round its waist.

symbols.concept: cone reconstruction of the tricuspid valve (Ebstein)
symbols.symbol: Einstein rolling the trident's displaced leaves into an ICE-CREAM CONE and sewing it back up at the proper ring

layers.meaning: the leaflets are freed, turned into a cone and re-attached at the true tricuspid annulus
layers.place: the tricuspid valve in Ebstein's anomaly

symbols.symbol: red doughnuts SMASHED to crumbs against a rough part of the pipe, the river turning dark cola-red

layers.meaning: red cells broken by pumps, a leaking or mechanical valve or a jet: dark urine, kidney injury
layers.place: where the jet or the pump hits them

symbols.notes: Classic in a paravalvular leak, a thrombosed VAD pump, a long bypass run.

symbols.symbol: in the icy water, the red doughnuts sticking together into CLUMPED lumps that block the small pipes

layers.meaning: antibodies that clump red cells in the cold: avoid deep hypothermia and cold cardioplegia, keep warm
layers.place: wherever the blood is cooled (cardioplegia, the bypass circuit)

symbols.symbol: every vase in the city gone LIMP and floppy like wet paper, the water pooling low; a bucket of bright blue paint (methylene blue) stiffens them again

layers.meaning: after bypass the vessels lose their tone: low pressure with a high cardiac output, needing pressors (or methylene blue)
layers.place: the arteries of the whole body

symbols.notes: The pressing hands (vasopressors) squeeze the limp vases.

symbols.symbol: a VACUUM CLEANER hose sealed over the opened, infected stern of the ship, sucking it clean until it can be closed

layers.meaning: suction under a sealed dressing removes fluid and helps granulation before sternal closure or a flap
layers.place: the open sternal wound

symbols.notes: Used for deep sternal wound infection (the stern rotting with green mould).

symbols.concept: transcatheter occluder devices (Amplatzer) for ASD, VSD, PFO, PDA
symbols.symbol: a pair of round silver CUFFLINKS clipped through the hole, one disc on each side of the wall

layers.meaning: a double-disc device delivered by catheter that clamps both sides of a hole
layers.place: through the hole in the party wall (or the duct)

symbols.notes: Needs rims of wall round the hole; a sinus venosus or primum hole (Venus, prime rib) cannot take one. Erosion: the disc rubbing through the orca.

symbols.symbol: a vampire COUNT in a black cape lifting the pipe of dollar bills over the orca and setting it down IN FRONT of it

layers.meaning: the pulmonary artery is brought anterior to the aorta during the arterial switch
layers.place: the great arteries

symbols.why: the Count lifts the pipe forward
symbols.notes: Alongside the switchman (arterial switch).

symbols.symbol: a small arching MUSCLE BRIDGE of red brick over the lad's slide, squeezing it flat with each beat

layers.meaning: a coronary segment (usually the LAD) runs inside the muscle and is squeezed in systole
layers.place: the middle of the LAD

symbols.notes: Usually harmless; surgery (unroofing or bypass) only for clear ischaemia.

symbols.symbol: a MAGPIE perched on a narrowed left flipper, stealing the water back down the lima bean vine (or up from the head) into the arm

layers.meaning: a narrowing at the start of the subclavian artery makes blood flow backwards from the vertebral artery, or from a LIMA graft, into the arm
layers.place: the left subclavian artery before the LIMA and vertebral branches

symbols.notes: Before or after CABG with a LIMA: angina when using the arm. Fixed by stenting or bypassing the flipper.

symbols.symbol: a technician touching the hotel's walls with a sparking BLUE WAND, trying to make the pirate start dancing

layers.meaning: catheters stimulate the heart to map its circuits and to see whether a dangerous rhythm can be provoked
layers.place: inside the heart's rooms

symbols.notes: MedCosmos drew the technician with the sparking blue wand five times.

symbols.concept: free wall rupture of the ventricle (after myocardial infarction)
symbols.symbol: the outer brick wall of the engine room BLOWN OUT, red water gushing into the aquarium round the hotel

layers.meaning: the infarcted wall tears through, usually within the first week: sudden tamponade
layers.place: the free wall of the left ventricle, into the pericardium

symbols.notes: The three mechanical complications of a heart attack: the hole in the lower party wall (VSD), the snapped pillar (papillary rupture), the blown-out wall.

symbols.symbol: the two leaves of the mitre meeting in a long firm HANDSHAKE

layers.meaning: the length over which the leaflets touch when closed; a good repair needs a long coaptation (at least about 5-8 mm)
layers.place: the closing edges of the valve leaflets

symbols.concept: infundibulum (conus, right ventricular outflow tract), infundibular stenosis
symbols.symbol: a kitchen FUNNEL leading from the blue engine room up into the pipe of dollar bills; in tetralogy its wall is pushed forward and squeezes it narrow

layers.meaning: the muscular outflow of the right ventricle below the pulmonary valve
layers.place: between the right ventricle and the pulmonary valve

symbols.notes: Tetralogy: the conal septum shifted forward narrows the funnel; muscle bundles are cut, or a patch widens it.

symbols.symbol: a small DRILLED HOLE in the stone basin of the fountain letting a little blue water spill into the red lobby

layers.meaning: a small hole from the Fontan pathway to the atrium: lowers the venous pressure and raises output at the cost of some blueness
layers.place: between the Fontan conduit and the atrium

symbols.notes: Closed later with the cufflinks if the child tolerates it.

symbols.concept: New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class
symbols.symbol: a man climbing the stairs of the EMPIRE STATE building: class I runs up freely, II tires on ordinary flights, III stops after a few steps, IV is breathless sitting at the bottom

layers.sound: NEW YORK Heart Association = the EMPIRE STATE building
layers.meaning: symptoms graded by how much activity brings breathlessness or tiredness
layers.place: the stairs of the Empire State building, the HART Hotel's neighbour

symbols.notes: Questions on surgery timing in valve disease often turn on it (class III-IV).

symbols.symbol: a bottle of WHISKY poured down a little septal branch of the crown into the bodybuilder's bulging biceps, which wilt

layers.meaning: absolute alcohol injected into a septal artery makes a controlled heart attack that thins the bulging septum in HCM
layers.place: the first septal branch of the LAD, into the upper septum

symbols.notes: Compare myectomy (the sculptor's chisel): alcohol leaves more heart block (the drawbridge) and suits older, frailer patients.

symbols.symbol: smooth WHITE TILES lining the inside of every pipe; where a tile falls off, sparks touch the river and a clot grows

layers.meaning: the living lining of the vessels: makes nitric oxide, keeps the blood from clotting; injured by bypass, smoking, high pressure
layers.place: the inner lining of all vessels

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew smooth white tiles lining a red pipe.

symbols.symbol: a round PATCH DOOR sewn into the scarred, ballooned part of the engine room's wall, shutting it off so the room is smaller again and keeps its proper shape

layers.meaning: excluding the dead, dilated part of the left ventricle with a circular patch to restore its size and shape
layers.place: the apex and front wall of the left ventricle after an anterior infarct

symbols.concept: penetrating cardiac injury and the cardiac box
symbols.symbol: a red DANGER BOX painted on the front of the chest, a dagger stuck inside it and red water filling the aquarium

layers.meaning: a wound inside the box (collarbones to costal margins, nipple to nipple) must be presumed to have hit the heart
layers.place: the front of the chest

symbols.notes: Then: tamponade (the flooding aquarium), subxiphoid window (the submarine), sternotomy or thoracotomy.

symbols.symbol: the red engine room shaped like a Japanese CLAY POT with a narrow neck and a ballooned round bottom (an octopus trap), after a shock

layers.meaning: after great stress the apex balloons and stops moving; mimics a heart attack with clean arteries; usually recovers
layers.place: the apex of the left ventricle

symbols.notes: Can follow surgery itself; watch for outflow obstruction (Uncle Sam).

symbols.symbol: a valve sewn from brown-and-white COW LEATHER, set into the doorway

layers.meaning: a tissue valve made from calf pericardium mounted on a frame; compare the pig (porcine) valve
layers.place: the aortic or mitral position

symbols.notes: Bovine pericardium is also a patch material (a strip of cow leather).

symbols.symbol: a silver STAR-shaped ball rattling inside a little BIRDCAGE set into the doorway

layers.meaning: the first durable mechanical valve: very thrombogenic, high gradient, needs strong anticoagulation
layers.place: the aortic or mitral position

symbols.why: a star ball in a cage
symbols.notes: Modern mechanical valves are bileaflet (the little steel robot).

symbols.symbol: the engine rooms stretched wide and floppy like an over-pulled ACCORDION that can barely squeeze a note

layers.meaning: big, thin-walled, weakly squeezing ventricles; the mitral ring stretches and leaks
layers.place: both ventricles, mostly the left

symbols.notes: Leads to the Vader (VAD) or the flowerpot (transplant).

symbols.symbol: a big leather BELLOWS pumping air down the ribbed hose into the sacks of dollar bills

layers.meaning: a machine breathes for the patient through a tube
layers.place: through the trachea into the lungs

symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins drew the bellows several times.

symbols.concept: Antibiotics (penicillin and the others; treatment and prophylaxis)
symbols.symbol: a giant PENCIL in Chopper's hand drawing a ring round the germs and crossing them out

layers.meaning: the pencil rings the germs and crosses them out: the drug kills them
layers.place: in Chopper's hand (the doctor), over the infected spot

symbols.why: PENCIL-lin; the pencil crosses the germs out
symbols.notes: Johns Hopkins 27 (actinomycosis) drew Chopper raising a giant pencil for penicillin; this makes it the symbol for every antibiotic. Prophylaxis: the pencil draws the ring before any germ arrives.

symbols.concept: Stem cells and cell therapy for the heart (bone marrow cells, mesenchymal cells, progenitor cells, myoblasts)
symbols.symbol: a gardener's tray of little green SEEDLINGS on long STEMS, planted into the grey scar of the red engine room's wall to grow new muscle there

layers.sound: STEM cells = seedlings on long STEMS
layers.meaning: a seedling can still grow into anything, as a stem cell can become new tissue
layers.place: planted into the scar of the engine room's wall, where muscle was lost

symbols.why: STEM cells drawn as seedlings on stems, planted into the scar
symbols.notes: The kind of cell is told by where the seedlings come from: scooped out of the red marrow of a cracked-open white bone (bone marrow cells), sprouting from a messy heap (MESS-enchymal cells), sprouting into tiny new pipes (endothelial progenitor cells), shaped like tiny skeletons (SKELETAL myoblasts), grown in the hotel's own window box (cardiac-derived cells). How they are given: poured from a watering can down the slides of the Liberty crown (intracoronary), injected through the wall (intramyocardial).

symbols.concept: Antigen-presenting cells (dendritic cells, macrophages) showing pieces of foreign protein to T cells; direct and indirect allorecognition
symbols.symbol: a TV PRESENTER with a microphone holding up pieces of a foreign plant's leaves on a little stand for the white soldier ants to see (one shelf = class I, two shelves = class II)

layers.meaning: it shows pieces of foreign protein to the T cells (the soldier ants), as a presenter shows things on air
layers.place: among the soldier ants beside the transplanted plant, holding the pieces up on a one- or two-shelf stand (MHC class I or II)

symbols.why: the name itself: an antigen-PRESENTING cell is a presenter; the stand's shelves keep MHC class I and II apart
symbols.notes: Direct allorecognition: the new plant's own presenters, who came with it, show its fresh leaves. Indirect: the patient's own presenters gather the fallen leaves, boil them down and show the pieces.

symbols.concept: mTOR (proliferation signal) inhibitors: sirolimus, everolimus; they stop cells from multiplying (G1 arrest), slow allograft vasculopathy and coat drug-eluting stents
symbols.symbol: a gardener's PRUNING HOOK snipping off every new shoot, so that nothing can grow and multiply: the overgrowing walls of the new crown's spikes, or the soldier ants' swarm

layers.meaning: it stops growth and multiplication, as pruning stops new shoots
layers.place: on the walls of the transplanted crown's spikes (vasculopathy), on the soldier ants' nest (rejection), on a Slinky's coat (drug-eluting stent)

symbols.why: pruning is what these drugs do to cells: they cut off proliferation
symbols.notes: Not a calcineurin inhibitor (the cyclone in a taco shell) and not an antimetabolite.

symbols.concept: Protein-losing enteropathy (after the Fontan operation): the gut leaks protein
symbols.symbol: a plate of SPAGHETTI (the gut) leaking white EGG-WHITE (protein) onto the table, usually beside the courtyard fountain (Fontan)

layers.meaning: egg-white is protein, and it leaks out
layers.place: the spaghetti is the gut (the mesenteric symbol's bowel), beside the Fontan fountain whose high water pressure causes it

symbols.why: what leaks (protein = egg-white) and where (the gut = spaghetti) in one object
symbols.notes: Late, uncommon and serious after a Fontan.

symbols.symbol: a little golden referee's WHISTLE with a round body

layers.sound: صفّارة (whistle) and صفّر (to whistle; in Iraq also 'to reset to zero': صفّر العدّاد) carry the letters of صِفر
layers.meaning: the referee's whistle starts every match at nil-nil: zero
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: صفّارة = صِفر; the kick-off whistle at 0-0; round like a 0
symbols.notes: Never a ring, coin or doughnut (the annulus, a lung coin, red cells) and never an egg (germ-cell tumour).

symbols.symbol: a little white UNICORN with one long straight golden horn

layers.sound: its Arabic name وحيد القرن begins with وحيد, the word واحد (one); English uni-corn = one horn
layers.meaning: one single horn
layers.shape: the horn stands straight up like a 1
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: وحيد القرن = واحد; one horn; uni = one; the horn is a 1
symbols.notes: Always white with a golden horn, no reins and no rainbow mane: the brown horse is the recurrent laryngeal nerve and the rainbow is the right coronary artery.

symbols.symbol: a little green DRAGON with two spread wings and a small flame, its neck curved like a 2

layers.sound: تِنّين (dragon) is how 'two' is said in the Levant (تنين) and close to Iraqi ثنين and اتنين
layers.meaning: two big wings
layers.shape: the curved neck and the tail flat on the ground make a 2
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: تنّين = اتنين; two wings; its neck curves like a 2
symbols.notes: Always with wings and flame, so it never reads as the brachiosaurus (brachiocephalic artery), which has neither.

symbols.symbol: a little red FOX with three bushy white-tipped tails

layers.sound: ثعلب is the ث word every Arab child learns (ث ثعلب), the letter that opens ثلاثة; English 'foxy'
layers.meaning: three tails
layers.shape: the three tails fan out side by side, three strokes
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: ث ثعلب = ثلاثة; three tails; foxy
symbols.notes: Always red-orange with exactly three tails: the grey wolf is WPW, the brown hare is heparin, and the purple foxglove flower is digoxin (a flower, never beside the fox).

symbols.symbol: a little black square GRADUATION CAP with a golden tassel

layers.sound: قبّعة rhymes with أربعة (-بعة), and it is مربّعة (square), from the same root as أربعة; English mortar-board ~ four
layers.meaning: a square: four corners
layers.shape: the flat square top has four corners
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: قبّعة مربّعة = أربعة; four corners; the cap thrown in the air when the boards are passed
symbols.notes: Never pointed (the bishop's mitre is the mitral valve) and never a crown (the coronaries).

symbols.symbol: a little blue HAMSA hand: an open palm with five fingers and an eye in its centre

layers.sound: its name is خمسة (خمسة وخميسة); English 'high five'
layers.meaning: five fingers
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: the amulet is called خمسة; five fingers; high five
symbols.notes: Always open, blue, with the eye: a fist is a fistula and a handshake is coaptation.

symbols.symbol: the SITT: a little lady in a GOLDEN GOWN, her long black hair ending in one round curl

layers.sound: ستّ (lady) is ستّة without its ة; in English, six sounds like sexy
layers.meaning: the lady of the house, الستّ
layers.shape: her hair falls into one round curl: a 6
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: الستّ = ستّة; six = sexy; her curl is a 6
symbols.notes: Always the golden gown and the curl, so she is not taken for a passer-by. Never red (the red dress is pericarditis), never white marble (Venus is sinus venosus), never on her toes (the ballerina is torsades).

symbols.symbol: a little SWIMMER diving off the end of a diving board, the board and his straight body making a 7

layers.sound: سبّاح is سبعة with a long ā: sab-bāḥ / sab-ʿa (ḥ and ʿ are twin sounds)
layers.meaning: the dive off the board
layers.shape: the flat board and his slanting body make a 7
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.notes: In the air or on the surface, never under water and never in a helmet (the deep-sea diver is mediastinoscopy). Write 'swimmer', never 'diver', in a prompt.

symbols.symbol: a little honey-brown VIOLIN, its body wide, narrow, wide

layers.meaning: its body has two round halves
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: كمان = ثمان; its curved body is an 8
symbols.notes: A violin alone: no orchestra or conductor (the sinus node) and no harp strings (the chordae).

symbols.symbol: a little brown MONKEY hanging by its curled tail, the loop of the tail on top: a 9

layers.sound: سعدان (monkey) carries the سع at the heart of تسعة
layers.meaning: a monkey hanging by its tail
layers.shape: the tail's loop on top and the hanging body make a 9
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.why: سعدان = تسعة; hanging by its tail it is a 9
symbols.notes: Never hanging from a bundle of branches (the conduction system).

symbols.concept: the decimal point in a number
symbols.symbol: a little GOLDEN DROP, set low between the whole and the fraction

layers.sound: in Arabic نقطة is both a drop and the decimal point (خمسة نقطة خمسة); in English a point is a dot
layers.meaning: a dot between the whole and the fraction
layers.place: drawn small and neat where it belongs in the scene: a tattoo on a hand or arm, a painting on a wall (a mural, a sign), or a design painted, carved or printed on an object, best on the thing whose value it gives; the digits stand side by side, the same size, left to right as a number is written, and the story names them in order

symbols.notes: Always golden and alone between two digits: drops of water or blood mean leaking (regurgitation).
